stays.note: Born 27 April 1926 in Roseville, Macomb County, Michigan to François (Frank) Kerbrat and Ozanna L'Herreaux, and enumerated there at age 3 with his parents and brother Yves (5) in the April 1930 US census.

Moved with his family from Michigan to California (where he and his brother Yves were issued consecutive California Social Security numbers 559-18-4798 and 559-18-4795) and lived in California until his death on 24 December 2000 with last residence in Needles, San Bernardino County, California (ZIP 92363).

Born 1 December 1920 in the downstairs room of the old house at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna as the third child of Dāvis Sirlaks and Alma Leontīne Āboltiņa, growing up at Vīstuči (where her paternal grandmother Marija I0008 died on 1 November 1925 and her maternal aunt Zelma Āboltiņa I1045 moved in 1929/1930 when Aina was in the 3rd grade) while herding cattle, attending the 4-year Dievabērns school in Jaunrauna (sleeping in its dormitory on winter weekdays) and grades 5–6 at Rauna parish school, and being confirmed by Pastor Arvīds Treicis at Rauna church in 1940.
Studied at Priekuļi Agricultural Secondary School ('Priekuļu Lauksaimniecības vidusskola'), graduating in 1940 before returning to Vīstuči and marrying Alberts Jurciņš in 1942.

Married Alberts Jurciņš in 1942 and moved with her dowry to his father's model farm 'Zvirgzdiņi' in Jaungulbene parish (the practice farm of the Priekuļi school); after fleeing briefly to Mazstraupe in 1944 when German troops evicted them and helping teacher Jānis Ambainis reopen the Priekuļi school in the winter of 1944–1945, she raised their sons Valdis (born 1947) and Alfrēds (born 1951) at Zvirgzdiņi, was widowed when Alberts died in late 1953, and worked in the kolkhoz and at the Dauksti village soviet in Gulbene district.

Fled from the kolkhoz with a pail of sauerkraut and a straw sack to work and sleep in the entrance hall of the Jaunpiebalga seed-control laboratory (where her younger sister Ilga Stangaine I1011 also lived and worked).

Settled in Priekuļi, where she worked in agricultural research as a scientist's assistant and amateur theatre director, walked from Priekuļi to Rauna and back on [day omitted] for Līva Voroņina's second birthday, helped restore nearby Lejas Vīstuči from 1 May 1993 onward, and completed her memoir 'Vīstuči' on 22 October 1998 before her death on 18 March 2001 (per the handwritten note in the memoir and Raimonds Voroņins's tree) or 18 March 2003 (per Timenote).

Resided with his wife Zelma Forstmane in Stūrmuiža parish, Tukums district, Courland, Latvia (adjacent to Vecauce/Auce) when their son Arvīds Fricis Danenbergs was born there on 17 January 1913 (4 January 1913 Julian); according to Peter's pre-2026 self-notes from his father's memories (summarized in docs/2026-revamp-proposal.md), Alberts taught mathematics in Zemgale and separated from the family when Arvīds was three years old.

Born 14 December 1916 in Russia ('Krievija', during the World War I Latvian refugee evacuation), as recorded in the Latvia, Rīga Internal Passport Holders Index (1918–1940, itemId 181080: 'Alberts Jēkabs Jurciņš | Dzimšana: 1916.gada 14. Dec - Krievija') and Raimonds Voroņins's tree.

Son of the owner of 'Zvirgzdiņi' in Jaungulbene parish (one of Latvia's 105 model farms and the practice farm of Priekuļi Agricultural Secondary School; he also held an interwar Rīga Prefecture internal passport in 1918–1940 and had his marriage banns with Aina Modrīte Sirlaka read at St Anne's Lutheran church in Jelgava in April 1942), where he married Aina in 1942, fled briefly with the household as far as Mazstraupe when evicted by German troops in 1944, and lived with Aina and their sons Valdis (born 1947) and Alfrēds (born 1951) until his death in late 1953 aged 36–37 (dated 26 October 1953 in Raimonds Voroņins's tree and recalled as November or December 1953 in Aina's memoir).

Born 2014 in California to Peter Charles Danenberg Jr. and Shayla Nadah Alamdari and raised with her parents and siblings in Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California; directly named as 'Aletheia, 18 months' in the 27 November / 17 December 2015 Palo Alto Weekly feature on Mountain View resident Shayla Danenberg's family.
Moved with her parents and siblings to a townhouse in Palo Alto, Santa Clara County, California in September 2022.
Born 1951 as the younger son of Alberts Jurciņš and Aina Modrīte Sirlaka at the Jurciņš family farm 'Zvirgzdiņi' in Jaungulbene parish, where his father died in late 1953.

Studied at and graduated from Priekuļi Technical School ('Priekuļu tehnikums', where his mother Aina lived and worked and from which his eldest son Artis also graduated by July 1995), married Dace Lauga, raised their children Artis (born 1976), Mārtiņš (born 1977), and Ilze (born 1984), and helped his uncle Valdis Sirlaks restore nearby Lejas Vīstuči in 1993–1995.

Born 16 March 1887 Jul. (28 March 1887 Greg.) in a bathhouse in Salaca parish as the twin sister of Alfrēds and daughter of the tailor Ancis Āboltiņš and Dārta Zariņa, grew up with her parents and siblings at their farm Ļekunkas in Salaca parish (giving her savings to buy out the farm), and entered domestic service at Salaca manor.

Worked in domestic service for wealthy families in Rīga (and spent one year looking after her employers' apartment in Switzerland while they were away), meeting her future husband Dāvis Sirlaks while both worked in Rīga.

After marrying Dāvis Sirlaks in Salaca church around 1915, she moved to his farm Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna, where she ran the household and dairy, bore and raised their five children (Jānis I1013, drowned 23 June 1918 aged 2; Velta I1009, left 1932/1935; Aina I1010, left 1935/1940; Ilga I1011, married and moved to Jaunpiebalga in 1952/1953; and Valdis I1012, left 1939/1945) alongside her mother-in-law Marija (I0008, until her death on 1 November 1925; sisters-in-law Kristīne I1035 and Anna I1006 and brother-in-law Reinholds I1036 left by 1919–1930) and her widowed sister Zelma Āboltiņa (I1045, who moved to Vīstuči in 1929/1930), and remained after Dāvis's death on 1 March 1952 until dying at Vīstuči in Ilga's care in early 1959 (dated 26 January 1959 in the memoir's family register and MyHeritage, recalled by Ilga as February 1959).
Born 17 November 1886 Jul. (29 November 1886 Greg.) near Cēsis ('Cēsu tuvumā').
Lived with her husband, the mason Kārlis Sirlaks (who died on 6 February 1957), in a courtyard flat on Pils iela in Cēsis, where they raised their daughters Ausma and Skaidrīte.
After her husband Kārlis died in February 1957, she spent her final years in Rīga (where her elder daughter Ausma Grīnberga lived with her family) and died there on 6 August 1968 aged 81.
Born 1987 as the daughter of Valdis Jurciņš and Ņina Panšina, growing up with her parents and older brother Māris at the Jurciņš family farm 'Zvirgzdiņi' in Jaungulbene parish (Gulbene district).
Married Justs Vucēns in Gulbene, Latvia on 30 June 2017.

Born 15 February 1839 Jul. (27 February 1839 Greg.) in Salaca Lutheran parish (Raduraksti 1:4:11:2055:2487:24454, frame 7, entry 17) and lived there until his marriage to Dārta Zariņa on 13/25 October 1874.

Married Dārta Zariņa in Salaca parish on 13/25 October 1874 and lived with her in Salaca parish (recorded at the Apiņi farm in Vecsalaca at daughter Zelma's October 1883 birth, and later at the family farm Ļekunkas near Salaca/Salacgrīva, bought out with daughter Alma's savings), working as a tailor and informal village teacher who taught 13 farmers' and farmhands' children to read and write.

Married Ruby Pershbaker (daughter of Adam Pershbaker, founder of nearby Prosper on the Coquille River in Coos County, Oregon) and had their daughter Edith Evelyn Muir on 21 December 1916, whose location in danenberg.sql is recorded as Coquille, Coos County, Oregon.

Moved with his wife Ruby Pershbaker from Coquille, Oregon to Los Gatos, Santa Clara County, California (enclosing place P-california; their daughter Edith Evelyn Muir graduated from Miss Harker's School in nearby Palo Alto and married Williamar Leslie at Stanford Memorial Chapel on 2 June 1941 as the 'daughter of Mr. and Mrs. A. R. Muir of Los Gatos').

Recorded in the 1857 Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 32) at Farm XIX Ģiboļi ('XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde', enclosed by P-priekuli) as 'dessen Frau Anne', aged 21 (born c. 1836; Raimonds Voroņins's tree gives 1829), wife of the co-farmer Jānis Ģibols, in the joint household with her brothers-in-law Mārcis (and his wife Anne) and Dāvis (transferred to the Rīga tax roll in 1856).

Recorded in the 1857 Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 32) at Farm XIX Ģiboļi ('XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde', enclosed by P-priekuli) as 'dessen Frau Anne', aged 38 (born c. 1819), wife of the farm head Mārcis Ģibols (whom she married in 1843 according to Raimonds Voroņins's tree), living in the joint household with her brothers-in-law Jānis (and his wife Anne) and Dāvis (transferred to the Rīga tax roll in 1856).

Born c. 1819–1822 at Farm No. 1 Mežciems ('No 1. Meschzeem', enclosed by P-priekuli) on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate, where she was enumerated in the 1826 surname revision (aged 4) and the 12 April 1834 soul revision (aged 11) with her parents Jānis Mežciems and Līze; married Mārcis Gibboy on 19/31 October 1847 and was enumerated on 13/25 September 1850 at Farm XIV Luste (enclosed by P-priekuli), aged 31.

Lived at the Kalna-Podis farm ('Freudenberg K. Pohdis') on the Priekuļi estate where her husband Mārcis worked as a farmhand when their daughter Marija was born there on 6/18 August 1853 and baptised on 16/28 August 1853.

Enumerated on 23 November / 5 December 1857 in the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 16) at Farm VI Rauguļi ('VI. Raugul Gesinde') as 'dessen Frau Anne', aged 38, with her husband Mārcis (50) and daughters Marija (4) and Kristīne (2).

Born 23 March 1890 Jul. (4 April 1890 Greg.) at Lejas Vīstuči ('Ronneb. Neuhof, Lj. Wihstuz') in Jaunrauna as the seventh child of Pēteris Sirlaks (I0007, who died on 22 November 1896) and Marija Gibboja (I0008, who died on 1 November 1925), grew up at Vīstuči, and retained her legal domicile ('piederības vieta') in Jaunrauna parish in the interwar Latvian passport index before settling in Rīga.

Lived in Rīga ('Rīgas tante'), where her niece Elvīra Sirlaka (I0006) lodged with her during her first university year (1930–1931) and where she owned a three-room flat at [address omitted], married the fireman Tīlmanis (I1042) in middle age, took in and raised her sister Ernestīne's surviving daughter Irma Piraineņa (I1038, arriving 1930/1945), and died of leukaemia on 29 December 1963 aged 73.

Born c. 1806/1807 and lived at Farm XIV Vīstuči ('Wihstuz', Family 58) on the Jaunrauna estate with her first husband, the farmer Peter Wihstuz (son of Jacob), and their children Marija (aged 8 in 1834), Liene (aged 2 in 1834), and Dāvis (born 1841), recorded there aged 27 in the 1834 Jaunrauna soul revision until Peter Wihstuz died in 1843.

Remained at Farm XIV Vīstuči after marrying her second husband Mārcis Sirlaks between 1843 and 1847, giving birth to their son Pēteris Sirlaks there on 10/22 August 1847 and recorded as 'dessen Frau Anne verwittwete Wihstuz' in the 9 October 1850 soul revision (aged 43) and the 8 February 1858 soul revision (aged 51).

Born on 3 September 1889 Jul. (15 September 1889 Greg.) at Ronneburg, Lappul (Lapuļi farm, Rauna manor) in Rauna parish to farmhand Dāvis Smukuls ('Kn. Dahw Smukkul') and Marija Kajone ('W. Mari gb. Kahjon'), and baptised in Rauna church on 8 September 1889 Jul. (20 September 1889 Greg., Rauna births 1889 no. 243).

Born c. 1742 and lived with his father Bērtulis at the Krīpēni farm (Strīķu Krīpēni, on the Strīķi / Strickenhof estate in Cēsis rural parish, enclosed by P-cesis), recorded as 'Krīpēnu Bērtuļa dēls Ansis' at his 1779 marriage in Cēsis rural parish.

Married Līze ('Ķienes Ērika meita Līze') in Cēsis rural parish in 1779 and lived with her at the Krīpēni farm on the Strīķi estate in Cēsis rural parish (where their son Bērtulis Balodis was born on 24 August 1782) until his death in 1803 aged 60–61, as noted in the 1811 Strīķi soul revision.

Born c. 1742 (aged 53 at the 1795 revision) and served as farm host ('Ansche 2ter Sohn Wirth') at Farm No. 6 Ģiboļi ('No 6. Gibboÿ Gesinde', enclosed by P-priekuli) on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate until his death in 1805 ('gestorben im Jahr 1805', August 1811 Priekuļi soul revision, LVVA 199/1/112, img 13).

Born 2013 in California to Peter Charles Danenberg Jr. and Shayla Nadah Alamdari while her father ran CrossFit Crown City (2011–2014) in Pasadena, Los Angeles County, California before the family moved to the Silicon Valley peninsula.

Lived with her parents and siblings in Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California after her father joined Google in 2013; directly named as 'Arete, 2' with her parents and siblings Kairos, Aletheia, and Chronos in the 17 December 2015 Palo Alto Weekly feature on Mountain View resident Shayla Danenberg's family.
Moved with her parents and siblings to a townhouse in Palo Alto, Santa Clara County, California in September 2022.

Born 1976 as the eldest child of Alfrēds Jurciņš and Dace Lauga, grew up in the Priekuļi area, graduated from Priekuļi Technical School ('Priekuļu tehnikums', greeted at its 85th jubilee on 8 July 1995 alongside his grandmother Aina and father Alfrēds as three generations of graduates), helped at the 1993–1995 family work-parties at nearby Lejas Vīstuči, and married Karīna Sproģe, with whom he had a son Arnis on 1998.
Born in 1950 in Latvia, had a son Ritvars (born 1979) with Ilze Stangaine, and died in 1991 aged 40–41 (buried at Rauna cemetery; his specific town or parish of residence in Latvia is not recorded).

Born 17 January 1913 (4 January 1913 Julian) in Stūrmuiža parish, Tukums district, Courland, Latvia (adjacent to Vecauce/Auce) to Alberts Danenbergs and Zelma Forstmane, as sworn on his 1950 Declaration of Intention ('Sturumuiza Latvia') and recorded on the 1947 Regensburg list ('Sturnonnischa [?]') and in his 1996 Daugavas Vanagu Mēnešraksts obituary ('Tukuma apriņķa Stūrmuižas pagastā').

Listed as 'Arvids Danenbergs no Penkules' (of Penkule parish) upon graduating from the Realschule section of the 2nd Jelgava State Gymnasium in July 1931; two months later, on 27 September 1931, his brother Žanis Danenbergs was recorded at the Dzērupi farm in Penkule parish.

Matriculated in September 1936 in the Agricultural Faculty in Jelgava (Jelgava Academy of Agriculture), lived in Jelgava during the academic years (returning to lectures in Jelgava in autumn 1937 while visiting Elvīra in Rīga on weekends), and remained registered in St Anne's Lutheran congregation in Jelgava (where his banns were read on 7 December 1941 and he was recorded as 'Arvīds Danenbergs no Jelgavas' in the 9 January 1942 Cēsu Vēstis church wedding notice).

Lived in his own quarters in Jaunjelgava during the summer of 1937 while surveying the banks of the Daugava for the Ķegums hydroelectric power station, where he met Elvīra Sirlaka (who was doing her summer pharmacy practice in Jaunjelgava).

Entered 'Stende, Kurzeme, Latvia' in Box 13 ('Last permanent residence or residence January 1, 1938') and 'In agricult. station' (the Stende agricultural selection station in Talsi district) on his 1945 Haunstetten DP-2 registration card; because his wife Elvīra and mother-in-law Emma also wrote 'Stende, Kurzeme, Latvia' in Box 13 of their DP-2 cards even though in January 1938 Elvīra lived in Rīga and Emma in Cēsis, this entry reflects either an agronomy practical-training stay at the Stende station during his Jelgava studies or his last pre-flight Talsi-district residence used uniformly across the family's UNRRA cards.

Worked at the Talsi agronomy bureau as the Talsi district agronomist until autumn 1944; Elvīra's memoir recounts that when she, her mother, Biruta, and Pēteris went to the Kurzeme coast in 1944 to await a boat to Sweden, 'Papa remained in Talsi, where he had his workplace,' before rejoining them to flee via Ventspils and Danzig to Germany.

After fleeing Latvia via Ventspils and Danzig in autumn 1944, he was assigned with his wife Elvīra, son Pēteris, and mother-in-law Emma to farm labour on two farms in Landkreis Regensburg, Bavaria (listed as 'Dipl. Landwirt' with sojourn date 12 January 1945 on the 1947 Landkreis Regensburg list), remaining there past the May 1945 surrender until moving to Haunstetten in summer 1945.

Lived with his family in a three-bedroom apartment in the Latvian DP camp at Haunstetten near Augsburg from August 1945 (first disinfestation 13 August 1945; DP-2 card dated 8 December 1945; twins Kalvis and Līga born 1946; sister-in-law Mirdza registered there from 23 July 1945 until emigrating to Canada in December 1948 / January 1949) until departing Haunstetten on 21 June 1949 for the Bremen-Grohn port transit camp (21–28 June 1949), while also earning a master's degree in agronomy from the Stuttgart-Hohenheim agricultural college.

After arriving in Boston on 7 July 1949, he lived and worked as a farm hand on the farm of sponsor Robert M. Hawk in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio (Rockford mailing address, where the Balks family joined the household in late January / February 1950), headed the nine-person household in the 10 April 1950 US Census, and swore his Declaration of Intention in Celina on 14 August 1950.

Left the Hawk farm after about a year for Tiffin, Seneca County, Ohio (already serving as Seneca County DHIA testing supervisor by 19 February 1951), residing in town at 23 Apple Street in 1953, naturalized in Toledo on 16 June 1955 as a resident of Tiffin, and farming on Rural Delivery 2, Box 77, Tiffin (purchased in 1955, listed in 1956–1959 R. L. Polk city directories, where he hosted a Latvian correspondence-school summer camp in July 1958 and was named in Tiffin in March 1960) until selling the Tiffin dairy farm and auctioning its 75 Holsteins and equipment on 21 April 1965 ('Having sold the farm we will sell everything else'); the upper bound is shortened from 1978 to 1975-08-09 because by 9 August 1975 he and Elvīra were already hosting the Latvian Agronomists' Society on their Michigan grain-corn farm.

After selling his Tiffin, Ohio dairy farm in April 1965, he farmed with his wife Elvīra in Decatur, Van Buren County, Michigan (referred to in Elvīra's memoir as 'the Decatur farm', where they hosted the Latvian Agronomists' Society meeting on their grain-corn farm near Marcellus/Decatur on 9 August 1975 — shortening the arrival upper bound from 1978 to 1975-08-09 — were listed at Decatur, Mich. on the March and May 1978 American Latvian Association life-member rolls, hosted Latvijas ciems Daugavas Vanagi meetings on their farm in 1984, 1986, and 1987, and were recorded at 17940 Dewey Lake Street, Decatur, MI 49045 on 1 August 1995 in the US Public Records Index).

Resided with his wife Elvīra on their property near Garezers at 56882 Point Road, Kelsey Lake, Cassopolis (LaGrange Township), Cass County, Michigan (recorded on 10 February 1996 and at his death on 19 February 1996, about six miles south of 17940 Dewey Lake Street, Decatur; he had served on the board of the regional Garezers 'Latvija' village Daugavas Vanagi branch since 1982).

Born 8 September 1923 and lived at the Vecozoli farm in Kraukļi parish, Madona district, Latvia until he was conscripted into the German army (Police Battalion no. 319, induction board at Cesvaine castle) in 1943.

Sent in May 1945 to a Soviet filtration camp at Komsomolsk-on-Amur in the Russian Far East ('filtrācijas nometni Sibīrijā - Komsomoļskā pie Amūras') before being transferred to Sillamäe in August 1947.
Served from 23 August 1947 to 1950 at Sillamäe, Estonia.
Identified at the time of his c. 1952–1953 courtship and marriage to Ilga Sirlaka in Aina Jurciņa's memoir (p. 32) as 'Arvīds Stangainis no Kraukļiem' (of Kraukļi).

Married Ilga Laimdota Sirlaka c. 1952–1953 and settled with her in Jaunpiebalga, Latvia, where they raised their daughters Ilze (born 1953) and Velta (born 1955, who lived with them in Jaunpiebalga until her marriage in Rauna on 11 June 1977) and where he died on 15 November 2005.

Born 30 May 1895 Jul. (11 June 1895 Greg.) at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna (baptised 9/21 July 1895 in Rauna church) as the eighth and youngest child of Pēteris Sirlaks (I0007, who died five months later on 22 November 1896) and Marija Gibboja (I0008), and raised at Vīstuči by his widowed mother.

Listed in Latvijas Vēstnesis (no. 178, 12 August 1922) as 'Augusts Pētera dēls Sirlaks' held in the Petrograd 2nd House of Correction ('Pēterpils 2. pārmācības namā', enclosed by P-russia) on the roll of imprisoned Latvian citizens in Soviet Russia to be exchanged.

Returned to Latvia after the 1922 prisoner exchange; his niece Aina Jurciņa recalled that he kept apart from the family as a communist, visited Vīstuči once in summer during the interwar republic carrying the newspaper Cīņa, and attended his sister Anna Tīlmane's funeral supper on Stabu iela in Rīga in December 1963 / January 1964 with his female companion.

Born 1968 (from the Ohio voter file); her Michigan birthplace is inferred from her father Dane Alden Greashaber's obituary (born 1928 in Milan, Monroe County, Michigan, married Irma Ann Burger in 1948, and worked for Kroger in Michigan for 21 years before moving his family to Marion, Ohio).
Moved with her parents Dane Alden Greashaber and Irma Ann Burger from Michigan to Marion, Marion County, Ohio (enclosed by P-ohio), where her father owned Dane's Fairpark Foodland for 11 years.

Has resided in Columbus, Franklin County, Ohio (enclosed by P-ohio) with her husband Justin Erik Danenbergs (who has lived in Columbus since graduating from Ohio State in 1999), registering to vote at their shared downtown Columbus residence on 16 August 2011 and named as 'Barbara (Justin) Danenbergs of Columbus, Oh.' in her father's April 2018 obituary.

Born 3 June 1919 in Cēsis after her parents Mārtiņš Sirlaks and Emma Smukule bought Lielā Katrīnas iela 13, grew up in Cēsis, and attended the Bērzaine secondary school for four years (while her eldest sister Elvīra I0006 left Cēsis for Rīga in autumn 1930).

Reported 'Rīga – Latvia' as her residence on 1 January 1938 on her 23 July 1945 Haunstetten DP-2 registration card, where she studied veterinary medicine (also working as assistant to the district veterinarian in Tukums before fleeing Latvia via the Kurzeme coast in autumn 1944).

After meeting Vitolds Balks on the Kurzeme coast in autumn 1944 and fleeing with him and the Danenberg/Sirlaks family via Ventspils and Danzig to Bavaria, she and Vitolds were assigned to wartime farm labour in Landkreis Kelheim (about a 30-minute train ride from the Danenbergs' farm in Landkreis Regensburg; recorded in the AOK Regensburg / Kelheim files from 1 January 1945 to 16 April 1945, in the Ausländeramt Kelheim personal files on 16 January 1945, and on the 17 June 1947 Landkreis Kelheim foreigner list); in spring 1945 they drove by horse and wagon into Regensburg to marry before moving to the Haunstetten DP camp in July 1945.

Registered on 23 July 1945 at the Haunstetten DP camp near Augsburg, sharing a three-bedroom apartment with her husband Vitolds, their daughter Ilze (born 1945 during Biruta's 5–15 November 1945 maternity stay at the Wöchnerinnen-Heim Augsburg / hospital in Hochfeld, Augsburg, where Biruta worked as a lab technician), her mother Emma Sirlaka, and the Danenberg family (where sister Mirdza was registered from 23 July 1945 until departing on 28 December 1948 and sailing from Bremen-Grohn for Canada on 13–14 January 1949, and from which Emma and the five Danenbergs departed for the USA on 21–22 June 1949), remaining at Haunstetten with Vitolds and Ilze until transferring to the Bremen-Grohn resettlement center on 9 January 1950.
