After selling the Tiffin, Ohio farm in April 1965, she lived with her husband Arvīds on their farm in Decatur, Van Buren County, Michigan ('while we were in the Decatur farm', memoir ¶19; hosting the Latvian Agronomists' Society meeting on their Michigan farm near Marcellus/Decatur on 9 August 1975 — shortening the arrival upper bound from 1978 to 1975-08-09 — listed at Decatur, Mich. in the March and May 1978 American Latvian Association life-member rolls, and recorded at 17940 Dewey Lake Street, Decatur, MI 49045 on 1 August 1995).

Lived with her husband Arvīds on their property near Garezers at 56882 Point Road, Kelsey Lake, Cassopolis (LaGrange Township), Cass County, Michigan (recorded on 10 February 1996 and as her home address at the time of the 19 February 1996 car crash that killed Arvīds and hospitalized her at Bronson Methodist Hospital in Kalamazoo before her transfer to a nursing home by 1 March 1996).

Moved after her husband Arvīds's February 1996 death to Milwaukee, Wisconsin (residing with and near her daughter Līga Schubach and son-in-law Wolf Schubach in Milwaukee, and at senior apartments at 4185 W Schroeder Dr Apt 310 in 1998–2004 and 9418 N Green Bay Rd Apt 137 c. 2005–2008), where she belonged to the Milwaukee Daugavas Vanagi branch and died on 18 June 2011 aged 99.

Born in 1907 or 1908 (1907 on the 1949 deportation list as daughter of Otto; 1908 on her gravestone and in the MyHeritage tree) into the Bēniņš family of the Gulbene area ('Emīlis savu sievu lūkot brauca gulbeniešos — Bēniņu dzimtā'), where she grew up before marrying Emīlis Sirlaks in 1930.

Married Emīlis Sirlaks in 1930 and lived with him, their son Harijs (born 1932), and Emīlis's parents Reinholds and Mīle at Kalna Vīstuči (Emīļmāja) in Jaunrauna until the family was deported on 25 March 1949 (case no. 12349).

Deported on 25 March 1949 with her husband Emīlis, son Harijs, and parents-in-law Reinholds (I1029, who died four weeks later on 20/22 April 1949) and Mīle from Vīstuči to Chainsky district ('Tomskas apg. Čajas raj.'), Tomsk oblast, Siberia (case no. 12349), remaining there in forced settlement until her release on 2 July 1956.

Returned with her husband Emīlis (I1032, who died in 1981) and mother-in-law Mīle (I1031, who died on 21 June 1958) after their 2 July 1956 release from Siberia to Kalna Vīstuči (Emīļmāja) in Jaunrauna, where she sewed Alma Sirlaka's burial dress and helped Ilga Sirlaka lay her out in January 1959, and lived there until her death in 1988.

people.name: Emma Smukule

stays.note: Born 25 December 1885 Jul. (6 January 1886 Greg.) at Lubar, farm Lj. Luhzmann[?], in Rauna Lutheran parish (recalled in her daughter Elvīra's memoir as Vecrauna), where her father Dahw Smukkul worked as a farmhand, and baptised in Rauna church by Pastor Dsirne on 2 February 1886 Jul. (14 February 1886 Greg., entry no. 33 'zweiten' beneath entry no. 32 'Februar zweiten').

Married Mārtiņš Vilhelms Sirlaks at St Martin's Lutheran church in Torņakalns, Rīga on 22 April 1911 Jul. (5 May 1911 Greg.), had their first daughter Elvīra there on 9 January 1912 (baptised at St Martin's on 3 March 1912), and lived in Torņakalns while her husband kept a tavern until World War I broke out in 1914.
Left Rīga at the start of World War I in 1914 and lived first in a rented house in the Vinterkalns area outside Cēsis, where her second daughter Mirdza was born on 17 January 1916.

By 1919 she and her husband Mārtiņš bought a house at Lielā Katrīnas iela 13 in Cēsis (where their third daughter Biruta was born on 3 June 1919 and the family survived the 1919 flu), ran a teahouse in Rožu laukums, and kept a grocery shop and bakery on Lielā Katrīnas iela where she baked bread for sale; daughter Elvīra lived there until moving to Rīga in autumn 1930 for university (later running the Litene pharmacy in 1941–1942), daughters Mirdza and Biruta lived there until moving to Rīga by 1 January 1938, and husband Mārtiņš lived there until his death in Cēsis on 30 December 1942, after which Emma remained in Latvia until fleeing with her daughters in autumn 1944.

After fleeing Latvia in autumn 1944 via the Kurzeme coast, Ventspils, and Danzig, she was assigned with Arvīds, Elvīra, and Pēteris to farm labour ('Landarbeiterin') on two farms in Landkreis Regensburg, Bavaria (sojourn date 12 January 1945 on the 1947 Landkreis Regensburg list), remaining there past the May 1945 surrender until moving to Haunstetten in summer 1945.

Lived with her daughters' families in a three-bedroom apartment at the Haunstetten DP camp near Augsburg (registered on her DP-2 card on 16 September 1945, where daughter Mirdza was registered from 23 July 1945 until emigrating to Canada in December 1948 / January 1949), caring for her grandchildren Pēteris, Ilze, and twins Kalvis and Līga until departing Haunstetten on 21 June 1949 for the Bremen-Grohn port transit camp (21–28 June 1949) while the Balks family remained at Haunstetten until 9 January 1950.

Although her separate last-minute emigration clearance listed her nominal destination as a housekeeper in 'Erie County, Ohio' (on row 1099 of the 28 June 1949 IRO nominal roll, case 39463, and line 17 of Manifest 48 at Boston on 7 July 1949), she travelled directly with the Danenbergs to the farm of sponsor Robert M. Hawk (and D. R. Smalley Farms, Rockford post office) in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio (where the Balks family joined them in late January / February 1950), was enumerated there in the 10 April 1950 US Census, and swore her Declaration of Intention in Celina on 14 August 1950.

Moved with the Danenberg family after about a year on the Hawk farm to Tiffin, Seneca County, Ohio (where Elvīra and Arvīds are recorded at 23 Apple Street in 1953 and on their Rural Delivery 2 Tiffin farm in 1956–1959 R. L. Polk city directories while Elvīra worked as a pharmacist at Mercy Hospital), helping raise Pēteris, Ilze, and the twins Kalvis and Līga while her daughters Elvīra and Biruta worked.

Her US Social Security Death Index entry records her last US residence at ZIP code 48075 in Southfield, Oakland County, Michigan (in the Detroit metropolitan area where her daughter Biruta Balka, son-in-law Vitolds Balks, and granddaughter Ilze lived), consistent with her Laiks obituary's statement that she lived alternately with her two daughters' families in the USA before spending her final years in Toronto.

Spent her final years ('pēdējos gados') in Toronto living with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law Fricis Gailītis (who died in September 1969), undergoing amputations of both legs before dying there on 9 October 1970 aged 85.

aka: Erna Smukul (1911 marriage list, a clerk's slip)

stays.note: Born in Mountain View on 2018 (Peter, 2 Nov 2026: 'Eos Adelaide Danenberg, 2018, Mountain View, CA'), where her parents and siblings were living until September 2022 (her father's and siblings' itineraries).
Moved with her parents and siblings to Palo Alto in September 2022 (her father's and siblings' itineraries); nothing records her living anywhere else.
Born 1953 with his provenance recorded as Youngstown, Mahoning County, Ohio in the 2015 database.

Married Sarah Pinkerton ('Pinkie') Fitz Gibbon and resided with her and their children in Berkeley, Alameda County, California (their oldest daughter Katie Flad, born 1987, later moved to Seattle, Washington by 2007 to attend the University of Washington): danenberg.sql records Berkeley ([phone omitted]) telephone numbers on his entry and notes that both he and Pinkie are ranked with the USTA Northern California section (ustanorcal.com).

Born 11 March 1860 Jul. (23 March 1860 Greg.) and baptised 20 March / 1 April 1860 at the Glāznieki farm ('Dubinsay Glahsneek') in Cēsis rural parish, where her parents Jānis Sirlaks and Līze Veidenbauma lived with Līze's family.
Lived as a child with her parents at the Jāņmuiža watermill ('Johannenhof Mühle'), where her father was the miller and her younger siblings Reinholds (1862) and Minna (1866) were born.
Moved as a child with her parents in 1869 to Kalna Vīstuči on the Jaunrauna estate when her father Jānis Sirlaks bought the farm.

Born 9 March 1879 Jul. (21 March 1879 Greg.) at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna (baptised at home, 'Get. vom K.V. Gudre im Hause / best. vom Past. Dsirne, in der K. am 15 April', on 19/31 March 1879 by churchwarden Gudre and ratified in Rauna church by Pastor Dsirne on 15/27 April 1879) as the second child of Pēteris Sirlaks and Marija Gibboja, and grew up at Vīstuči (where her elder sister Natālija I1007 died on 14 June 1887 aged 12 and her father Pēteris I0007 died on 22 November 1896).

After marrying the Finn Johans Pirainens and having four children (Irma, Viktors, Aksels, and Rūriks), she was deported or displaced in the Soviet Union and died of starvation in Siberia ('Ernestīne mirusi bada nāvē Sibirijā'), while her husband and three sons died in Karelia.

people.name: Estella May Alderson

stays.note: Born 5 May 1916 in Seattle, King County, Washington as Phillis May Barns to Irene Barns (WA birth certificate 146-1916-005906, filed 12 May 1916) before being taken in by Winter Scott Alderson and Carrie May Newman of Portland.

Raised in Portland by her adoptive parents Winter Scott Alderson (who died in February 1933) and Carrie May Newman: enumerated there in the 1920 census (222 East 7th Street) and the 1930 census (5003 52nd Avenue S.E.), and enrolled in Portland Public Schools in 1922–1923 (cited on her 1952 delayed birth certificate).

Married William S. (Sherwin William) Rowley on 30 December 1933 across the river in Vancouver, Washington, and the 1940 census records both their 1935 residences as Portland, Multnomah County, Oregon.

Enumerated in the 1940 census as Stella May Rowley (age 23) with her first husband Sherwin William Rowley (age 24) in Concord Election Precinct, Clackamas County, Oregon (Sheet 5A, lines 13–14, Household 106), immediately next door to her adoptive mother Carrie May Schroeder and Charles Schroeder (Sheet 5A, lines 11–12, Household 105), and recorded as 'Mrs. Stella Rowley, Milwaukie' (the mailing town for Concord) in the 14 March 1944 obituary of her adoptive brother Elmer E. Alderson.

Her 11 May 1946 Clark County marriage statistics record states she had lived in Portland for the past six months; the June 1950 census enumerates her as Steela M. Hall (age 33) in Multnomah County, Oregon with her husband Charles H. Hall (29), daughter Kathleen D. Hall (3, born in Oregon) and son Steven C. Hall (0, born June 1949 in Oregon), and she swore her delayed birth certificate application in Portland on 13 March 1952. The 1950 census (6 April 1950, ED 26-76, sheet 12, lines 15–18) has the household at 3904 S.E. 115th Avenue, Multnomah County (read from the whole census sheet, 2026-11-09).
The 11 August 1970 obituary of her adoptive mother Carrie M. Schroeder (died 9 August 1970) records 'Mrs. Stella Hall of Akron, Ohio' as residing in Akron, Summit County, Ohio on 9 August 1970.

Public-records index (U.S. Public Records Index, 1950-1993) gives Stella M Hall (born 5 May 1916) at 4337 Cesano Ct, Palo Alto (1981) and 4094 Villa Vis, Palo Alto, with a later address in Upland, San Bernardino County (1993); the same addresses as her husband Charles H Hall.
Her husband Charles Henry Hall died in Santa Ana on 9 March 2001 and his 16 March 2001 obituary describes him as of Newport Coast (Orange County, California), survived by his wife Stella.

She died in San Diego, California on 6 June 2008, and the Social Security Death Index (JGVL-W6X, with death certificate observed) records her last residence ZIP code as 92116 in the city of San Diego.

aka: Phillis May Barns (her birth name: WA birth certificate 146-1916-005906)

stays.note: Born in April 1963 (per his TruePeopleSearch capture and 1963 in the 2015 database) with provenance recorded as Abadan, Iran in the 2015 database, before the Alamdari family emigrated to Southern California.
Married Jeanne M. Kerbrat in Los Angeles, California on 20 April 1985, as recorded in the California Marriage Index (1960–1985).

Recorded in his TruePeopleSearch capture at a residence in Monrovia, Los Angeles County, California in November–December 1985 (shortly after daughter Shayla's October 1985 birth, explaining his [phone omitted] San Gabriel Valley landline).

Lived with his wife Jeanne and daughter Shayla in La Verne, Los Angeles County, California for about 31 years (recorded at one La Verne residence from October 1986 to December 1993 and a second La Verne house from October 1995 to June 2018 in his TruePeopleSearch capture, with a [phone omitted] La Verne landline).

Settled with his wife Jeanne in Morgan Hill, Santa Clara County, California, where he worked as a school bus driver for the Morgan Hill Unified School District in 2016–2020 and purchased a condominium in January/March 2019 where they reside in 2026.

Born 30 November 1881 in Brittany (Bretagne), France: the 2015 database records his birth in 1881 and provenance in Bretagne, and his NUMIDENT record in the Kerbrat Social Security index records 'KERBRAT, FRANK was born 30 November 1881 in France'.

Lived with his wife Ozanna L'Herreaux (Ozanna Lheureux, born 3 May 1896) and sons Yves John Kerbrat (born 13 October 1924) and Adrien F. Kerbrat in Roseville, Macomb County, Michigan on 27 April 1926, when Adrien's birth in Roseville, Michigan is recorded in the NUMIDENT index.

Moved with his wife Ozanna and sons Yves J. and Adrien F. Kerbrat from Michigan to the Santa Monica area of Los Angeles County, California, where he was assigned California Social Security number 550-26-2558, his sons received sequential California SSNs (559-18-4795 and 559-18-4798) before 1950, and the Santa Monica Social Security field office received his claim on 22 July 1952 and his wife Ozanna's claim on 16 January 1956.

Born 6 January 1907 in Matkule parish, Tukums district, Courland, Latvia to Fricis Gailītis and Lizete Novadnieks, as recorded on his 27 August 1945 AEF DP-2 registration card (which identifies him as 'Mag. math., ģimn. skolotājs' — the mathematics teacher who emigrated to Canada in 1948 and married Mirdza Sirlaka in Toronto in May 1955).

After graduating with a Master of Mathematics from the University of Latvia, he worked as a teacher in Latvia from 1929 (teaching mathematics at Rīga City 2nd Gymnasium) and is recorded on his 27 August 1945 DP-2 card with last permanent residence (1 January 1938) in Rīga, Latvia ('Mag. math., ģimn. skolotājs').

Registered on 27 August 1945 as a Latvian displaced person at Assembly Center Hanau 27 (Hanau, Hesse, Germany; Reg. No. G11095303), where he taught at the Latvian gymnasium in Hanau before emigrating to Canada in 1948 on PCIRO roll 81739047 (row 363, certificate PC 20238).

Emigrated from Germany to Canada in 1948 as a single DP and worked his compulsory one-year contract on 'Hydro' construction works before settling in Toronto (upper bound shortened from 1955-05 because his July 1955 Laiks interview states he attended Toronto Central Technical School evening classes for five years after his contract year).

Moved to Toronto after completing his one-year Hydro labour contract (working as a carpenter while attending Toronto Central Technical School evening classes for five years, graduating from the Ontario College of Education in spring 1955, marrying Mirdza Sirlaka in Toronto in May 1955, teaching mathematics at Danforth Technical School from autumn 1955, serving as treasurer of St Andrew's Latvian congregation, and joined in his final years by his mother-in-law Emma Sirlaka) until his death at Sunnybrook Hospital in Toronto on 23 September 1969.

Recorded with provenance New Orleans, Louisiana in the 2015 database as the daughter of Tristram Stuart Fitz Gibbon and Jessica Urban Nelson (though Tristram has no New Orleans record of his own, and it is unknown when between 1988 and May 2006 she moved to California); the US Public Records Index entry attached to Peter Charles Danenberg Jr. in the MyHeritage GEDCOM gives her birth date as 1988, agreeing with Spokeo's 'Age 38' in October 2026.

Recorded in the US Public Records Index (in the MyHeritage GEDCOM) at a residence in Altadena, Los Angeles County, California on 11 May 2006 with Peter Charles Danenberg Jr. (whom she married on 10 September 2006, and with whom she had daughter Mneme in 2007), where Kathleen D. Danenberg is listed as an associated relative; the Spokeo browser capture also links her with Peter and Līga Danenberg at the Danenberg parents' Altadena residence (2006–2022).

Recorded in the Spokeo browser capture at a condominium in Monrovia, Los Angeles County, California from 2012 to 2020 while working on independent short films (2015–2016) and co-authoring a February 2018 prostate-cancer research abstract at the USC Norris Comprehensive Cancer Center in Los Angeles.
Recorded in the Spokeo browser capture at a house in Alhambra, Los Angeles County, California from 2019 to 2022 (with an Alhambra [phone omitted] telephone number).

Recorded in the Spokeo browser capture at a second condominium in Monrovia, Los Angeles County, California from 2020 as her current residence (with undated public-records associations in Palo Alto, California and Sedona/Cottonwood, Arizona).

Moved with her parents Antoni and Maria Magdalena Symanski to Los Angeles by 1930 and married Harold Gerard Urban in California on 9 January 1945 (residing with him in Burbank, Los Angeles County in the 1950 census).

Born 28 April 1886/1887 in Fossil, Gilliam County, Oregon (NUMIDENT 6KW1-MWL6 gives 28 Apr 1887 in Fossil, Gilliam, OR; 1900 census MMPL-98T gives Apr 1886 in OR) and lived there with his parents and siblings.
Enumerated at age 14 ('G C Newman', born April 1886 in Oregon) in his parents' household in Toroda Creek Precinct, Okanogan County, Washington in the 1900 census.

Married widow AnnaBelle (Rice) Coffman in Spokane, Washington on 29 October 1918 (giving his residence as Okanogan County), registered for Social Security in September 1937, and resided in Tonasket, Okanogan County, Washington until his death on 30 August 1949.

Born 1932 at Kalna Vīstuči (Emīļmāja) in Jaunrauna to Emīlis Sirlaks and Elza (née Bēniņa), and lived there with his parents and grandparents Reinholds and Mīle until the family was deported on 25 March 1949 (case no. 12349).

Deported at age 17 on 25 March 1949 with his parents and grandparents Reinholds (I1029, who died four weeks later on 20/22 April 1949) and Mīle from Vīstuči to Chainsky district ('Tomskas apg. Čajas raj.'), Tomsk oblast, Siberia (case no. 12349), where he was held in forced settlement until his release on 2 July 1956.

Returned to Latvia after his 2 July 1956 release from Siberia and lived in Priekuļi ('Harija Sirlaka, dzīv. Priekuļos' in Aina Jurciņa's 1998 memoir, p. 8) with his wife Dzintra and children until his death on 12 November 2004.

Born in Albany, Albany County, New York; her 1924 Washington death certificate (N3GL-VV8, HVW8-656Z) and gravestone (QVKJ-HGH7) give her birth date as 26 September 1847 in Albany, N.Y., whereas FamilySearch tree L6VS-97W gives 22 November 1848.

Lived in Lyndonville ('Lindenville', Town of Yates), Orleans County, New York with her husband Edward Newman when their eldest son Edward Newman Jr. was born there on 3 July 1875 (NUMIDENT 6KWT-VKSP and 1945 WA death record HVF9-N9ZM; July 1874 in the 1900 census MMPL-98T).
Lived in Oak Orchard, Ridgeway, Orleans County, New York with her husband Edward Newman when their daughter Carrie May Newman was born there on 24 May 1878.
Enumerated with her husband Edward, son Edward (4) and daughter May (2) in Ash Rock Township, Rooks County, Kansas in the 1880 census.
Moved west via California, where her son William Newman was born in March 1882 according to the 1900 census (MMPL-98T).

Lived in Fossil, Gilliam County, Oregon, where her children Lilly E. Newman (born 1882/Jan 1884 in Fossil) and Grover Cleveland Newman (born 28 April 1886/1887 in Fossil) were born and from where her daughter Carrie May Newman eloped in August 1892.
Enumerated with her husband Edward and children Edward, William, L. A. and G. C. Newman in Toroda Creek, Okanogan County, Washington in the 1900 census.

Her husband Edward Newman died in Conconully, Okanogan County, Washington on 24 July 1909, and on 2 August 1909 her son Ed Newman Jr. brought her back from a visit to her daughter in Portland, Oregon to Oroville in Okanogan County, Washington.

Following her husband's July 1909 death, she was enumerated on 23 April 1910 as 'Hattie Newman, mother-in-law, 61' in the household of her daughter May C. Alderson and son-in-law Winter S. Alderson in Milwaukie, Clackamas County, Oregon.

Returned to Okanogan County, Washington, where she died in Tonasket (where her sons Edward Newman Jr. and Grover Cleveland Newman lived) on 29 April 1924 and was buried at Tonasket Cemetery on 30 April 1924.

Born 1922 in the downstairs room of the old house at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna as the fourth child of Dāvis Sirlaks and Alma Leontīne Āboltiņa, grew up at Vīstuči (where her paternal grandmother Marija I0008 died on 1 November 1925 and her maternal aunt Zelma Āboltiņa I1045 moved in 1929/1930), attended the 4-year Dievabērns school in Jaunrauna and grades 5–6 at Rauna parish school (c. 1936/1937), and then worked for five years at Vīstuči to help pay the interest on the Land Bank loan ('Piecus gadus pēc skolas Ilga strādā Vīstučos', memoir p. 51) before taking the entrance examinations for the Ranka housekeeping school.

After working five years at Vīstuči following primary school, she travelled to take the entrance examinations at the two-year Ranka housekeeping school ('Rankas mājturības skola', memoir p. 51, where Laimonis Hofmanis explained a mathematics problem on the way that appeared on the exam) and completed the two-year course as one of 30 admitted out of 80 applicants (celebrating her 20th birthday at home at Vīstuči on 10 November 1942).

Lived at Lejas Vīstuči before her marriage, working at the seed-control laboratory in nearby Rauna (and briefly at a milk-and-bread shop in Cēsis after her father had her struck off the Vīstuči register to reduce Soviet taxes).

Married Arvīds Stangainis around 1952–1953 (when she was nearly 30) and settled with him in Jaunpiebalga, where she worked in the bookshop and the seed-control laboratory (joined there for a time after 1953 by her widowed sister Aina Jurciņa I1010), raised their daughters Ilze (born 1953) and Velta (born 1955, who lived there until her 1977 marriage in Rauna), cared for her dying mother (1959), aunt Zelma (1960), and brother Valdis (1995) at Vīstuči, helped restore Vīstuči from 1993 onward, and lived with Arvīds until his death on 15 November 2005 and her own death on 7 January 2011 aged 88.

Born 1945 at the hospital in Hochfeld, Augsburg while her parents Vitolds and Biruta Balks lived with her grandmother Emma Sirlaka and the Danenberg family in the Haunstetten DP camp (where her aunt Mirdza was registered from 23 July 1945 until emigrating to Canada in December 1948 / January 1949, and from which Emma and the five Danenbergs departed for the USA on 21–22 June 1949), remaining at Haunstetten with her parents until transferring to the Bremen-Grohn resettlement center on 9 January 1950.

Transferred from Assembly Center Haunstetten no. 505 on 9 January 1950 to the IRO Resettlement Center at Bremen-Grohn with her parents Vitolds and Biruta before sailing for New York on USS General Howze on 22 January 1950.

After arriving in New York on USS General Howze in late January / February 1950, she lived with her parents, grandmother Emma, and the Danenberg family in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio (Rockford mailing address), where she was enumerated as 'Ilze Balks' (age 4) in the 10 April 1950 US Census and where her mother applied for an Ohio Social Security number in February 1951.

Lived with her parents Vitolds and Biruta Balks in the Southfield, Oakland County, Michigan area, where her grandmother Emma Sirlaka's US Social Security Death Index record gives her last US residence at ZIP code 48075 in Southfield (before Emma moved to Toronto in 1965/1969-09 and died in October 1970); the upper bound is shortened from 1971/1973-09-01 to 1965/1970 because she studied pharmacy at Ohio State University in Columbus, graduating with a B.S. in 1970.

Attended Ohio State University in Columbus, Ohio, serving as president of the OSU student pharmacy association chapter in her final year of study and graduating with a B.S. in pharmacy in 1970 as 'Ilze Balka Augenberga'.

Resided in Beverly Hills, Oakland County, Michigan with her husband Jānis Uģis Augenbergs and their daughters Inga (born 1971) and Ivete (born 1973), recorded there in the US Public Records Index from 1 September 1973 and in the Detroit area in her father's September 1984 obituary until moving to Farmington by 1 October 1992 (while daughter Ivete remained recorded at the Beverly Hills residence on 1 February 1994).

Recorded in the US Public Records Index as residing in Farmington, Oakland County, Michigan from 1 October 1992 (in a separate condominium unit and with a separate telephone listing from her former husband Jānis Uģis Augenbergs, who was recorded in another unit in July–November 2004; she had married Walter Valdis Bērziņš by March 1996, when she spoke as Ilze Bērziņa at her uncle Arvīds Danenbergs's memorial service, maintaining Oakland County telephone listings through 5 December 2008).
Born 1959 as the daughter of Valdis Laimdots Sirlaks (chief engineer of the Priekuļi Selection Station) and Valda Katlapa, growing up with her parents and older brother Jānis in Priekuļi.
Studied medicine in Rīga, receiving her physician's diploma ('ārstes diploms') at the Rīga Opera on 29 June 1983.

Lived and worked as a physician in Latvia, marrying Jānis Veinbergs, raising their daughter Ieva (born 1987) and twin sons Ingmārs and Krišjānis (born 1990), and regularly taking part in the 1993–1997 restoration work-parties and farming at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna.

Born 1981 in Rīga (at a maternity hospital) as the second child of Pēteris Voroņins and Velta Stangaine, and grew up with her parents, older brother Raimonds (I1053, who spent his entire childhood in Rauna, voronins-tree.ged line 124, before moving to Rīga in 1996/2017), and younger sister Līva (I1248, born 1990) in Rauna.
Lives in Rīga with her partner/husband Einārs Dzirjānis and their children Luīze Dzirjāne (born 2013 in Rīga) and Olivers Dzirjānis (born 2018 in Rīga).

people.name: Irene Mary Barnhart
aka: Irene M. Larson (m. 1940 Benjamin Arthur Larson)

stays.note: After her mother Ernestīne died of starvation in Siberia and her father Johans Pirainens and brothers Viktors, Aksels, and Rūriks died in Karelia, she made her way starved and in rags to her maternal aunt Anna Tīlmane (née Sirlaka, I1006, who died on 29 December 1963) at Stabu iela 46/48 in Rīga, who took her in and raised her as a daughter; Irma remained in Rīga, where she had her daughter Regīna and where Aina Jurciņa later mailed her parents' wedding photograph.

Born 1973 to Jānis Uģis Augenbergs and Ilze Balka while her parents resided in Beverly Hills, Oakland County, Michigan (from at least 1 September 1973; her mother Ilze is recorded in Farmington from 1 October 1992), directly recorded at the family's Beverly Hills residence in the US Public Records Index on 1 February 1994 at age 20, and listed as 'Ivete Augenbergs, Beverly Hills' when awarded an Oakland University scholarship on 24 November 1994.

Resided in Troy, Oakland County, Michigan with her husband Ezequiel Jorge Larroquette, recorded in the US Public Records Index in Troy on 2 November 2004 and with a Troy telephone listing from 1 June 2002 to 20 August 2008.

Born in 1964 to Yves John Kerbrat and Carol May Nolen while her father lived in the San Fernando Valley (Van Nuys and Sylmar) in Los Angeles, California, and married Fathollah Alamdari in Los Angeles on 20 April 1985 (recorded in the California Marriage Index 1960–1985).
Lived with her husband Fathollah Alamdari and newborn daughter Shayla in Monrovia, Los Angeles County, California in November–December 1985 (per Fathollah's TruePeopleSearch capture).

Lived with her husband Fathollah and daughter Shayla in La Verne, Los Angeles County, California from October 1986 to June 2018 (recorded at two La Verne houses in Fathollah's and Shayla's TruePeopleSearch captures and corroborated by La Verne on Jeanne's OpenPayrolls background snippet).

Settled with her husband Fathollah Alamdari at a condominium in Morgan Hill, Santa Clara County, California while working for Santa Clara County Schools and as Purchasing Agent at Gavilan College in nearby Gilroy (2020–2026).

A Finn ('soms Johans Johana dēls Pirainens'), husband of Ernestīne Sirlaka and father of Irma, Viktors, Aksels, and Rūriks; he and his three sons lived and died in Karelia ('Vīrs un dēli miruši Karēlijā') during the Soviet period while Ernestīne died of starvation in Siberia.

Born 1975 (recorded in the Ohio voter file, whereas the 2015 database and MyHeritage tree give 1976) and raised in Midland (Jefferson Township), Clinton County, Ohio by his parents Kalvis Danenbergs and Melinda Lee Berger, who have resided and been registered to vote in Midland continuously since 28 September 1973.
Moved to Columbus, Franklin County, Ohio in 1994 to attend The Ohio State University, residing in the Stadium Scholarship Dormitory and earning his B.S. in Pharmacy in 1999.

Purchased a home in Powell, Delaware County, Ohio (a northern suburb of Columbus) jointly with Barbara L. Greashaber, as reported in The Columbus Dispatch on 8 September 2001, before registering to vote in Columbus in 2011.

Has resided in Columbus, Franklin County, Ohio with his wife Barbara L. Greashaber since at least August/September 2011 (when both registered to vote at their shared Columbus residence) while working as a pharmacist for Medco, Accredo, and Express Scripts.
Married Alīna Jurciņa in Gulbene, Latvia on 30 June 2017.

Married Velta Skaidrīte Sirlaka in the Latvian Lutheran congregation in Hamilton, Ontario in June 1955 (reported in Latvija Amerikā on 22 June 1955) and lived with her in their own house in Ontario (also wintering in Florida).

Lived in his later years with his wife Velta in St. Catharines, Ontario (where Velta died at Tufford Manor Nursing Home in March 2015 and had her funeral at Hulse & English Funeral Home & Chapel as 'beloved wife of the late Janis'), until his death on 1 April 2012 aged 96.

Born c. 1786 (aged 9 in 1795, 25 in 1811, 40 in 1826) and lived his entire life at Farm No. 1 Mežciems ('No 1. Meschzeem', enclosed by P-priekuli) on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate with his father Jēkabs Mežciems, wife Līze, and children until his death in 1833 ('1833 gestorben', 1834 Priekuļi soul revision).

people.name: Jānis Sirlaks

stays.note: Born 8/20 May 1829 at the Lejas-Spāriņi farm ('Spāriņos') on the Jaunrauna estate to the manor weaver Jānis Sirlaks and Masche, and enumerated there at age 4 on 11 May 1834 in the Jaunrauna soul revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 156, Family 4) before entering manor service at Jaunrauna.

Enumerated at age 20 on 9 October 1850 in the Jaunrauna soul revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, frame 220, fol. 207, Family 15) among the manor people ('Hofsleute') of Jaunrauna ('Ronneburg-Neuhof'), where Emīlis Sirlaks recalled he served as a footman ('sulainis') and the 17/29 April 1855 Cēsis rural marriage register (no. 14) records the groom as a gardener at Jaunrauna ('Ronneburg Neuhof Gärtner').
Lived with his wife Līze Veidenbauma at her family's Glāznieki farm ('Dubinsay Glahsneek') in Cēsis rural parish when their eldest daughter Ernestīne Sirlaka was born there on 11/23 March 1860.

Worked as the miller ('Müller Jahnis Sirlak') at the Jāņmuiža watermill ('Johannenhof Mühle') in Cēsis rural parish (now Priekuļi parish), where his son Reinholds was born on 8/20 September 1862 and his daughter Minna on 24 February / 8 March 1866.

Bought the Kalna Vīstuči homestead on the Jaunrauna estate from Mārcis Vīstucis in 1869 (initially sharing a house with his elder brother Mārcis Sirlaks on the Emīļmāja site) and farmed there with his wife Līze, children Ernestīne (I1028, until 1869/1880), Reinholds (I1029), and Minna (I1030, until 1869/1890), daughter-in-law Mīle (I1031, from 1894/1900), and grandchildren until his death on 20 February / 5 March 1901.

aka: Sirlak Jonh (Rauna church book, per the memoir)

stays.note: Born in 1916 at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna as the first-born child of Dāvis Sirlaks and Alma Leontīne Āboltiņa (where his 1916 silver christening spoon was unearthed on 1 May 1993) and lived there with his parents and paternal grandmother Marija until he drowned in the pond on Līgo day (23 June) 1918 aged two.

Born on Līgo evening, 1956 (when his aunt Aina Jurciņa visited him on the first day of his life), as the son of Valdis Laimdots Sirlaks (chief engineer of the Priekuļi Selection Station) and Valda Katlapa, growing up with his parents and younger sister Inga (who left in 1977 to study medicine in Rīga) in Priekuļi.

Restorer of the ancestral farm Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna (to whom Aina Jurciņa dedicated her 1998 memoir), leading the orchard-planting and restoration work-parties from 1 May 1993 (while his father Valdis lived in the barn room until his death on 11/12 October 1995), rebuilding the second storey in 1995 and moving into his newly finished upstairs room alongside his mother Valda's room at Christmas 1995, receiving the land-register certificate ('zemesgrāmata') around 15 June 1996, and continuing to rebuild the house and grounds with his wife Daina and son Dāvis through 1998.
Born c. 1779 and recorded at Farm no. 7 Staļi on the Jaunrauna (Ronneburg-Neuhof) estate (enclosed by P-jaunrauna) at the 1795 soul revision aged 16, as noted in the 1811 Jaunrauna soul revision.
Recorded in the 1811 Jaunrauna soul revision (and in the 'previous revision' column of the 1816 revision) at Farm no. 29 Lejas-Spāriņi ('a. d. No. 29') as a farmhand aged 32.

Enumerated in the 1816 Jaunrauna soul revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 31) among the manor people ('Hofsleute') at Jaunrauna manor as manor weaver ('Weber Jahn, Ansch S., a. d. No. 29'), aged 37, with his wife Masche (41) and infant son Dāvis (aged ½).

Moved from the manor people ('aus Hofsleute') back to Farm XXIX Lejas-Spāriņi ('Leis Sparing', Family 4), where his youngest son Jānis Sirlaks was born on 8/20 May 1829 and where the 1834 Jaunrauna soul revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 156) records that 'Sillak Jahn, Ansche Sohn, Hofsweber' died in 1830.

Recorded in the 1857 Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 32) at Farm XIX Ģiboļi ('XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde', enclosed by P-priekuli) as '2. Jahn Wirthshälftner' (half-tenant / co-farmer, second son of Jahn), aged 28 at the 1850 revision and 35 in 1857 (born c. 1822), living there with his elder brother Mārcis, his younger brother Dāvis (until 1856), his wife Anne (aged 21), and his son Mārcis (born 1855, aged 2).

Born c. 1758 (aged 38 in 1795, 54 in 1811, 68 in 1826) and served as farm host ('Wirth Jacob Jahns Sohn Meschzeem') at Farm No. 1 Mežciems ('No 1. Meschzeem', enclosed by P-priekuli) on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate until his death in 1832 ('1832 gestorben', 1834 Priekuļi soul revision).
Born 2012 in California to Peter Charles Danenberg Jr. and Shayla Nadah Alamdari while his father ran CrossFit Crown City (2011–2014) and lived in Pasadena, Los Angeles County, California.

Moved with his parents to Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California after his father joined Google in 2013; directly named as 'Kairos, 3' with his parents and siblings Arete, Aletheia, and Chronos in the 17 December 2015 Palo Alto Weekly feature on Mountain View resident Shayla Danenberg's family.
Moved with his parents and siblings to a townhouse in Palo Alto, Santa Clara County, California in September 2022.

Born 1946 (with his twin sister Līga) in Augsburg while his family lived at the Haunstetten DP camp (where his aunt Mirdza was registered from 23 July 1945 until emigrating to Canada in December 1948 / January 1949), remaining there with his parents, elder brother Pēteris, grandmother Emma, and the Balks family until departing Haunstetten on 21 June 1949 for the Bremen-Grohn port transit camp (21–28 June 1949).

After landing in Boston on 7 July 1949, he lived with his family on the farm of sponsor Robert M. Hawk in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio (Rockford mailing address, where the Balks family joined them in late January / February 1950), enumerated as 'Kalvis V Danenbergs' (age 3) in the 10 April 1950 US Census.

Moved with his parents, brother, twin sister, and grandmother after about a year on the Hawk farm to Tiffin, Seneca County, Ohio (where his parents are recorded in 1953, 1956, 1958, and 1959 Tiffin city directories while his mother worked as a pharmacist at Mercy Hospital in Tiffin and his father bought a Seneca County farm in 1955 and sold it in April 1965), attending Hopewell-Loudon School in nearby Bascom, Seneca County from elementary school (third grade in 1955–1956) through his senior year of high school in 1964–1965 (named a National Merit semifinalist on 24 September 1964 and Ohio General Scholarship Test honorable mention on 21 December 1964).

Lived in Columbus, Franklin County, Ohio while studying pharmacy (recorded as a 24-year-old student residing at [address omitted], Columbus in the 3 January 1971 Columbus Dispatch marriage-licence notice for his marriage to Melinda L. Berger, replacing the previous unplaced gap between his 1965 Hopewell-Loudon graduation and his 28 September 1973 Clinton County voter registration).

Has resided in Midland (Jefferson Township), Clinton County, Ohio with his wife Melinda Lee Berger since at least 28 September 1973 (when both registered to vote in Clinton County; also signed a 31 July 2010 Toledo Blade guest-book entry from Midland, Ohio), raising their son Justin there from his birth on 1975 until he left for college in Columbus in 1994, working as clinical coordinator and registered pharmacist at Clinton Memorial Hospital in nearby Wilmington, and earning an M.S. in pharmacology and biology at Wright State University in Dayton in June 1986.

Born 1947 in Oregon to Charles Henry Hall and Estella May Alderson; directly enumerated as Kathleen D. Hall (age 3, born in Oregon) with her parents and younger brother Steven C. Hall (age 0, born June 1949 in Oregon) in Multnomah County, Oregon in the June 1950 census, and her mother swore her delayed birth certificate application in Portland on 13 March 1952. The 1950 census (6 April 1950, ED 26-76, sheet 12, lines 15–18) has the household at [address omitted], Multnomah County (read from the whole census sheet, 2026-11-09).
Lived in Santa Barbara, California with her husband Peter Valentins Danenbergs during his doctoral studies at UC Santa Barbara (1966–1970); their daughter Līga was born in Santa Barbara on 1966.
Married Peter Valentins Danenbergs in Los Angeles on 23 April 1966 while he was completing his M.S. and working as an assistant at the University of Southern California.

Lived in Madison, Wisconsin with her husband while he worked at the McArdle Laboratory and Wisconsin Clinical Cancer Center (1970–1976) and while she earned her B.S. in biochemistry at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

Moved back to Los Angeles in 1976 when her husband joined the USC School of Medicine faculty; co-authored papers at USC in 1977–1978 and had their son Peter in Los Angeles on 1978 before settling in nearby La Cañada Flintridge.

Recorded in the family's MyHeritage tree with a residence at [address omitted], La Cañada Flintridge, Los Angeles County, while her daughter Līga attended nearby Glendale High School (graduating in 1984) and before the family moved to Pasadena by 1 January 1988.
Recorded as residing in Pasadena, Los Angeles County, California on 1 January 1988 while serving as Laboratory Director at USC.

Resided in Altadena, Los Angeles County, California (where her husband was recorded by February 1996, and on her 2007–2012 SEC EDGAR filer record and the MyHeritage tree; son Peter lived there until 1995 and daughter Līga until 1 September 1996) until the house was lost in the Eaton Fire of 7–8 January 2025.
After losing the Altadena house in the January 2025 Eaton Fire, she lists Los Angeles, California on her verified LinkedIn profile in 2026.

Born 31 December 1855 Jul. (12 January 1856 Greg.) and baptised 6/18 January 1856 at Kalna-Podis / Podiņi ('Freudenberg K. Pohding', Cēsis rural births 1855 no. 214) to farmhand Mārcis Gibboy and Anne before the family moved to Farm VI Rauguļi by December 1857.

Born c. 1855 and enumerated on 23 November / 5 December 1857 in the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 16) at Farm VI Rauguļi ('VI. Raugul Gesinde') as '2. Christine, 2' alongside her parents Mārcis Gibboy (50) and Anne (38) and her elder sister Marija (4).

Probably the Kristīne Gibboy who stood godmother as a maid ('M. Kristine Gibboy') at the December 1883 baptism of her sister Marija's son Mārtiņš Vilhelms Sirlaks at Lejas-Vīstuči and who, as the wife of the bricklayer/mason Jānis Karnītis ('132. Neuhof, Lj. Wihstuz / Jahnis Karniht. / Elt. Maurer Jahn Karnicht u. Frau Kristine gb. Gibboi. beide lutherisch.'), gave birth to a son Jānis Karnītis at Lejas Vīstuči ('Neuhof, Lj. Wihstuz', her sister Marija and brother-in-law Pēteris Sirlaks's homestead) on 27 May / 8 June 1888 at 8 p.m. (baptised at home, 'Get. vom K.V. Sirlak im Hause', on 29 May / 10 June 1888 by churchwarden Sirlak, with godparents bachelor Reinwald [Reinholds] Sirlak, farm-mistress Anna Sirlak, and widow Anna Blizzan).

Born 9 April 1888 Jul. (21 April 1888 Greg.) at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna (baptised at home, 'Get. v. Wth Dahw Gudre im Hause', on Easter Monday 25 April / 7 May 1888 by farmer Dāvis Gudre, with godparents farm-mistress Mari Sirnis, farmhand Jahn Karniht, and maid Mari Karnit) as the sixth child of Pēteris Sirlaks and Marija Gibboja, and lived at Vīstuči (where her father Pēteris I0007 died on 22 November 1896) through at least the June 1919 Battle of Cēsis, when she ran across the Lejas meadows from Vīstuči to Liepa to direct Latvian artillery fire onto the German position in Kaulu birze.

Born 21 February 1881 Jul. (5 March 1881 Greg.) at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna (baptised at home, 'Get. vom Past. Dsirne im Hause', on 24 February / 8 March 1881 by Pastor Dsirne) as the third child of Pēteris Sirlaks and Marija Gibboja, and grew up at Vīstuči (where his elder sister Natālija I1007 died on 14 June 1887 aged 12 and his father Pēteris I0007 died on 22 November 1896).

Lived with his wife Alvīne (née Vītiņa) in a pleasant flat in the courtyard house on Pils iela in Cēsis ('Mūsu tēva brālis Kārlis dzīvoja Cēsīs Pils ielas sētas mājas jaukā dzīvoklī'), working as a bricklayer/mason and raising their daughters Ausma and Skaidrīte; he also built the Rauna Society house and visited Skaidrīte where she practised as the Rauna dentist ('Es jau neatnācu pie Raunas zobārstes, bet gan pie savas meitas'), dying in Rauna on 6 February 1957 aged 75.

Born 1946 (with her twin brother Kalvis) in Augsburg while her family lived at the Haunstetten DP camp (where her aunt Mirdza was registered from 23 July 1945 until emigrating to Canada in December 1948 / January 1949), remaining there with her parents, elder brother Pēteris, grandmother Emma, and the Balks family until departing Haunstetten on 21 June 1949 for the Bremen-Grohn port transit camp (21–28 June 1949).

After landing in Boston on 7 July 1949, she lived with her family on the farm of sponsor Robert M. Hawk in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio (Rockford mailing address, where the Balks family joined them in late January / February 1950), enumerated as 'Liga Danenbergs' (age 3) in the 10 April 1950 US Census.

Moved with her parents, brothers, and grandmother after about a year on the Hawk farm to Tiffin, Seneca County, Ohio (where her parents are recorded in 1953, 1956, 1958, and 1959 Tiffin city directories while her mother worked as a pharmacist at Mercy Hospital in Tiffin and her father bought a Seneca County farm in 1955), attending third grade (in Mrs Pauline Fruth's class) at Hopewell-Loudon School in nearby Bascom, Seneca County in 1955–1956.

Moved to Milwaukee, Wisconsin after marrying Wolfhart K. ('Wolf') Schubach in 1968 or 1969, where she earned a Master of Arts degree in library and information science from the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee in June 1971, worked as one of the first two women weights-and-measures inspectors for the Milwaukee Health Department in summer 1971, served as a Milwaukee Public Library librarian (appearing on Channel 10's Critique in 1978), co-founded EXACTA Corporation (1976, Brookfield) and Exacta Graphics, Inc. (1985, Butler), lived with Wolf until his death on 15 March 2019 (and where her mother Elvīra Danenbergs, I0006, is also recorded at their Milwaukee home in the US Public Records Index during her 1996/1998–2011 Milwaukee years), and has continued to reside.

Born 1966 in Santa Barbara, California, where her father was a doctoral student and research assistant at UC Santa Barbara (1966–1970); her Facebook profile names Santa Barbara as her hometown and [day omitted] as her birthday, matching the US Public Records Index.

Lived as a child (aged 3 to 9) in Madison, Wisconsin with her parents while her father worked at the McArdle Laboratory and Wisconsin Clinical Cancer Center (1970–1976) and her mother completed her B.S. in biochemistry at the University of Wisconsin–Madison.

Moved with her parents to Los Angeles in 1976 when her father joined the USC School of Medicine faculty; her brother Peter was born in Los Angeles on 1978 before the family settled in nearby La Cañada Flintridge.

Lived with her parents and brother in La Cañada Flintridge, Los Angeles County, California (recorded on her mother in the MyHeritage family tree) while attending nearby Glendale High School, from which she graduated in 1984.
Earned her B.S.E.E. and M.S. in Computer Engineering at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles (where an undated residence beside USC in ZIP 90007 is recorded in the MyHeritage tree).

Recorded in the US Public Records Index at her parents' longtime residence in Altadena, Los Angeles County, California (ZIP 91001; its 626-791 landline remained associated with her in a 1 July 2008 phone-index refresh) prior to moving into her own Los Angeles apartment in September 1996.
Recorded in the US Public Records Index as residing in Los Angeles (ZIP 90046) from 1 September 1996 while working at Skunk New Media in Santa Monica (from February 1996).

Recorded in the US Public Records Index as residing in West Hollywood, Los Angeles County, California (ZIP 90069) from 1 April 1997 (and on the adjacent Los Angeles/West Hollywood border in ZIP 90046 through 12 July 2001) while working at Sony Online Entertainment in Culver City (1997–2000) and PacketVideo in Los Angeles (2000–2002) and beginning her MBA at USC in 2001.

Recorded in the US Public Records Index with an address in Oakland, Alameda County, California (ZIP 94618) dated 12 July 2001, though her LinkedIn profile states she worked full-time at PacketVideo in Los Angeles from June 2000 to January 2002 and began her USC MBA in Los Angeles in 2001 (and the 510 telephone listing of the same date shares the identical 7-digit number as her 213/323 West Hollywood line, suggesting either a brief 2002 Bay Area stay or an aggregator concatenation).

Recorded in the US Public Records Index with an undated residence in San Francisco, California (ZIP 94131) in the MyHeritage family tree, possibly from 2002 (between leaving PacketVideo in January 2002 and joining Capitol Records in Hollywood in February 2003) or an undated secondary address.

Recorded in the US Public Records Index as residing in West Hollywood, Los Angeles County, California (ZIP 90069) from 1 February 2003, corroborated by her California Secretary of State corporate filing for Starwood Sober Living, Inc. (incorporated 25 March 2003, inactive 1 November 2005) naming her at the same West Hollywood residential address.
Recorded in the US Public Records Index as residing in La Crescenta, Los Angeles County, California (ZIP 91214) from 1 May 2006 while serving as IT Director at Response Genetics in Los Angeles.

Recorded in the US Public Records Index at a second residence on the same road in La Crescenta, Los Angeles County, California (ZIP 91214) between 1 June and 22 July 2008 (with a La Crescenta 818-248 telephone listing dated 22 July 2008), corroborated by her California Secretary of State corporate filing for NutraSculpt Inc. (incorporated 29 May 2012 at that same La Crescenta address, active until 2018/2019).
Resides in Los Angeles, California as of October 2026, as listed on both her LinkedIn and Facebook profiles.

people.name: Lilly E. Newman

stays.note: Born in Fossil, Gilliam County, Oregon (January 1884 in the 1900 census MMPL-98T; age 19 in March 1901 on her BC marriage registration JD8G-HXW, which names her birthplace as Fossil, Oregon) and grew up there with her parents and siblings.

Enumerated at age 16 ('L E Newman', born January 1884 in Oregon) in her parents' household in Toroda Creek Precinct, Okanogan County, Washington in the 1900 census before moving just across the border to Rossland, British Columbia.
Married bachelor Edelbert M. Harthorn in Rossland, Kootenay District, British Columbia, Canada on 26 March 1901 (BC Marriage Registration 01-09-165783, JD8G-HXW).

aka: Lilly E. Harthorn (m. 1901 Edelbert M. Harthorn)

stays.note: Born 19 June 1893 in Oregon to Winter Scott Alderson and Carrie May Newman; her Oregon birth records give the county variously as Umatilla County (HR3B-1P2M) and Wheeler County (W7J8-HGN2; Wheeler County was created in 1899 from territory including Fossil).
Her younger brother Elmer Elsworth Alderson was born on 22 October 1895 in Portland, Oregon according to his Oregon birth record (84KN-27MM) and 1944 Oregon death certificate (ZNLQ-YFPZ).

Enumerated at age 17 in the 23 April 1910 census in her parents' household in Milwaukie, Clackamas County, Oregon, with her brother Elmer and maternal grandmother Hattie Newman, next door to her future husband Charles W. Helgerson.
Married to Charles W. Helgerson and living in Tacoma, Pierce County, Washington on 14–15 January 1914 when their infant was born and died.
Her son Ronald C. Helgerson was born in Washington in 1922 according to the 1930 and 1940 US censuses.
Registered to vote as Lola Helgerson in Multnomah County (Portland), Oregon in 1928 (1:1:W94Y-763Z).
Enumerated as Lola G. Helgerson in Los Angeles, California in the 1930 census (1:1:XCVY-4NH) with her husband Charles Helgerson and son Ronald C. Helgerson.

Registered to vote in Multnomah County, Oregon in 1935 (1:1:W94Y-76W2) and enumerated as Lolla Helgerson in Tract 52, Portland, Multnomah County, Oregon in the 1940 census (1:1:VRTV-T2T, with 1935 residence at Same Place) with husband Charles Helgerson and son Ronald Helgerson, before marrying Anson A. Webster across the river in Clark County, Washington on 30 June 1941.
Resided in Newport, Lincoln County, Oregon (enclosing place P-oregon) as 'Mrs. Lola Webster, Newport' at the death of her brother Elmer E. Alderson on 12 March 1944.
Resided in Lebanon, Linn County, Oregon under her later married name 'Mrs. Lola West of Lebanon, Ore.' when her mother Carrie M. Schroeder died in Lebanon on 9 August 1970.

Resided at the end of her life in Salem, Marion County, Oregon (enclosing place P-oregon, ZIP 97306), where the Social Security Death Index records her last known residence at her death as Lola West in December 1984 aged 91.
Born 2013 in Rīga as the daughter of Einārs Dzirjānis and Inga Voroņina, and lives there with her parents and younger brother Olivers (born 2018 in Rīga).

Born 1990 in the maternity hospital at the district seat of Cēsis as the youngest child of Pēteris Voroņins and Velta Stangaine, and grew up with her parents and older siblings Raimonds (I1053, who moved to Rīga in 1996/2017) and Inga (I1242, who moved to Rīga in 1998/2013) in Rauna, where her great-aunt Aina Jurciņa walked on foot from Priekuļi to Rauna and back on her second birthday (1992) and where she helped with the 1997 family work-parties at Lejas Vīstuči.

Married Ansis of the Krīpēni farm ('Krīpēnu Bērtuļa dēls Ansis') in Cēsis rural parish in 1779 and lived with him at Strīķu Krīpēni on the Strīķi estate in Cēsis rural parish, where their son Bērtulis Balodis was born on 24 August 1782.

Born c. 1786 (aged 40 in 1826, widow aged 47 in 1834) and lived at Farm No. 1 Mežciems ('No 1. Meschzeem', enclosed by P-priekuli) on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate with her husband Jānis Mežciems (d. 1833) and daughter Anne.

Born 14/26 June 1836 at the Glāznieki farm ('Glahsneek', Cēsis rural parish), daughter of the farm head ('Glahsneek Wirths T. Lihse Weidenbaum' at her 17/29 April 1855 marriage), and continued living there with her husband Jānis Sirlaks through at least 11/23 March 1860, when their eldest daughter Ernestīne was born at Glāznieki.

Lived with her husband Jānis Sirlaks at the Jāņmuiža watermill ('Johannenhof Mühle'), where he was the miller and where their son Reinholds was born on 8/20 September 1862 and their daughter Minna on 24 February / 8 March 1866.

Moved with her husband Jānis Sirlaks (I1026, who died on 5 March 1901) to Kalna Vīstuči in Jaunrauna when he bought the farm in 1869, living there with her children Ernestīne (I1028, until 1869/1880), Reinholds (I1029), and Minna (I1030, until 1869/1890), daughter-in-law Mīle (I1031, from 1894/1900), and grandchildren until her death on 24 December 1901 Jul. (6 January 1902 Greg.).

Born 6 January 1919 at St. Joseph Hospital in Vancouver, Clark County, Washington, enumerated there at age 1 with her parents on 7 January 1920, and lived there with them at least through her sister Catherine's birth at home on 12 February 1922.

Enumerated at age 11 in April 1930 in her mother Susie Hall's household in Portland, Oregon, and her 24 September 1938 marriage return (at North Bonneville, Skamania County, Washington, to Robert H. Elfsten) gives her residence as Portland. The 1930 census (7 April 1930) has the household at 1225 S. Leonard Street, St. Johns, Portland; the 1950 census (13 April 1950, ED 37-553, sheet 6) at 9727 N. Willamette Blvd. (both read from the whole census sheets, 2026-11-09).

Resided in Hacienda Heights, Los Angeles County, California (enclosing place P-los-angeles, ZIP 91745) from at least 9 October 1966 (when her son Charles Arthur Elfsten's wedding announcement in the Los Angeles Herald Examiner identified her as 'Mrs. Doyle Henry of Hacienda Heights') until her death in June 1978 aged 59, when the Social Security Death Index recorded her last known residence as ZIP 91745 (Hacienda Heights, Los Angeles County, California).

Born 6 August 1853 Jul. (18 August 1853 Greg.) at the Kalna-Podis farm ('Freudenberg K. Pohdis') on the Priekuļi estate, where her father Mārcis Gibboy worked as a farmhand ('Lett. Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij') and her mother Anne lived, and baptised in the Cēsis Latvian rural congregation on 16/28 August 1853.

Enumerated at age 4 ('Töchter 1. Marri, 4') on 23 November / 5 December 1857 in the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 16) at Farm VI Rauguļi ('VI. Raugul Gesinde') with her parents Mārcis Gibboy (50) and Anne (38) and her younger sister Kristīne (2).

Married Pēteris Sirlaks at Rauna church on 10/22 February 1874 and lived with him at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna, where all eight of their children were born between 1875 and 1895 (eldest daughter Natālija I1007 died on 14 June 1887 aged 12; Marija's sister Kristīne I1302 also resided at Lejas Vīstuči as the wife of mason Jānis Karnītis in 1883/1888-06-10), until Pēteris's death on 10/22 November 1896.

Remained at Lejas Vīstuči for 29 years as a widow after Pēteris Sirlaks's death in November 1896, raising her seven surviving children (of whom Mārtiņš I0003 left by 1900/1911-05-05, Ernestīne I1033 by 1896/1912, Kārlis I1034 by 1896/1925, Reinholds I1036 by 1910/1922-08-12, Kristīne I1035 after June 1919, and Anna I1006 by 1918/1930) and later living in the downstairs room with her son Dāvis Sirlaks (I1005, returned 1911/1915), his wife Alma (I1008, married 1915), and their children (son Jānis I1013 drowned on 23 June 1918 aged 2; Velta I1009, Aina I1010, Ilga I1011, and Valdis I1012 were born 1919–1924) until her death at Vīstuči in November 1925 aged 72.

people.name: Marija Kajone

stays.note: Married Dahw Smukkul in Rauna Lutheran parish on 28 October 1884 Jul. (9 November 1884 Greg., Rauna marriages 1884 no. 42), lived with him at Lubar, farm Lj. Luhzmann[?], in Rauna parish when their daughter Emma was born on 25 December 1885 Jul. (6 January 1886 Greg.) and baptised on 2 February 1886 Jul. (14 February 1886 Greg., entry no. 33), and lived at Ronneburg, Lappul (Lapuļi farm, Rauna manor) when their younger daughter Anna Smukkul was born on 3 September 1889 Jul. (15 September 1889 Greg.) and baptised on 8 September 1889 Jul. (20 September 1889 Greg., Rauna births 1889 no. 243).

aka: Marie geb. Kahjon (1886 baptism of Emma)

stays.note: Born 2 July 1802 in Lexington, Rockbridge County, Virginia.

Married Charles Royal in Miami County, Ohio (dated 14 March 1820 in Ohio county marriage records XD7X-D8M and XDPV-38N, vs. 12 March 1819 at Piqua on FamilySearch tree LHKT-Y2F), lived with him in neighbouring Springcreek Township, Miami County in the 1820 census (XHLQ-HLV), and remained in Ohio through the birth of son James S. Royal in 1829 (1850 census M85T-M9V).

Lived with her husband Charles Royal in Fountain County, Indiana in the 1830 census (XHGG-VWP) and remained in Indiana through the births of daughter Elizabeth (1832) and son Charles Fletcher Royal (1834/1835, per M85T-M9V and C2WZ-34N2).

Moved with her husband to northern Illinois by 3 September 1837 (when son William McKindsie Royal was born in Chicago, Cook County, Illinois per HV4G-B2T2 and M85T-M9V), and had daughter Mary Catharine Royal on 25 January 1842 in Fox River, LaSalle County (or Cook County), Illinois.
Enumerated with her husband and six children (including Mary Catharine) in Mazon, Grundy County, Illinois in the 1850 census (M85T-M9V) before crossing overland to Oregon Territory in 1852.
Enumerated with her husband and four children in Sandy Precinct, Multnomah County, Oregon in the 1860 census (MDQJ-TLR).
Enumerated with her husband Charles Royal and son Louis B. Royal in Albany, Linn County, Oregon in the 1870 census (MF8Y-VVY).

Enumerated as widowed grandmother Mary A. Royal (age 79) in the household of her daughter Mary C. Alderson, son-in-law Christopher Alderson and grandson Winter S. Alderson in Sheridan, Yamhill County, Oregon in the 1880 census (MNCR-WFG).
Died in Portland, Multnomah County, Oregon on 25 December 1888.
Born 25 January 1842 in Fox River, LaSalle County, Illinois (or Cook County, Illinois in her 1928 obituary QP1T-26BQ) to Charles Royal and Mary Ann Gearhart.
Enumerated at age 9 with her parents and five siblings in Mazon, Grundy County, Illinois in the 1850 census before the family crossed overland to Oregon Territory in 1852.
Enumerated at age 17 with her parents in Sandy Precinct, Multnomah County, Oregon in the 1860 census.
Married Reverend Christopher Alderson in Portland, Multnomah County, Oregon on 13 August 1862.
Her eldest son William C. Alderson was born in Washington Territory in 1864 according to the 1880 census (MNCR-WFG) and his 1928 Oregon death certificate (CGNN-5HZM).
Her son Winter Scott Alderson was born in Springwater, Clackamas County, Oregon on 1 December 1866.
Her daughter Edith Ruth Alderson was born at Empire, Coos County, Oregon on 30 April 1869.
Enumerated with her husband Christopher and children Charles W., Winter S. and Edith R. in Jackson County, Oregon in the 1870 census.
Her daughter Anna Alderson Pearson was born in Wilbur, Douglas County, Oregon in 1872 according to her 1947 Oregon death certificate (ZV3F-D9W2).
Enumerated with her husband Christopher, six children including Winter Scott, and her widowed mother Mary A. Royal in Sheridan, Yamhill County, Oregon in the 1880 census.

Her youngest daughter Lois E. Alderson was born in Salem, Marion County, Oregon on 15 November 1886, and she was enumerated with her husband Christopher and four daughters in Salem Election Precinct 4, Marion County in the 1900 census.

Lived in Portland, Multnomah County, Oregon from at least 1907 (with her husband Christopher before his October 1907 death) through the 1910 census (Portland Ward 8, 1208 Belmont Street, with daughters Edith and Lois) and October 1928 until her death in Portland on 30 December 1928.
Born c. 1882/1883 in Makawao, Maui, Hawaii ('A native of Makawao, Hawaii, age 84 years' in her 25 June 1967 death notice, matching her Maui provenance in the 2015 database).

Resided in Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California from at least 2 June 1941 ('Mrs. Mary E. Leslie of Mountain View' at her son Williamar Leslie's Stanford wedding) until her death in Mountain View on 24 June 1967 aged 84, when her San Jose Mercury News death notice recorded her residence at 465 Loreto St., Mountain View.
Born in Penrith, Cumberland, England and baptised on 14 January 1801 at St Andrew's Church, Penrith.

Married Christopher Alderson on 4 June 1823 at Appleby St Michael, Westmorland and lived with him at Brackenber in Bongate (Appleby St Michael parish) through the 1841 (with son Christopher, who emigrated in 1848), 1851 and 1861 censuses until her death at Appleby on 1 October 1864.

Born c. 1776 (aged 50 in 1826, widow aged 57 in 1834) and lived at Farm No. 1 Mežciems ('No 1. Meschzeem', enclosed by P-priekuli) on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate with her husband Jēkabs Mežciems (d. 1832).

Born 1947 (date recorded in the Ohio voter file without a birthplace) and raised in the Blanchester area of Clinton County, Ohio (enclosing place P-ohio), graduating from Blanchester High School in Blanchester, Ohio in the Class of 1965.
Resided in Columbus, Franklin County, Ohio at age 23 when she and Kalvis Danenbergs applied for a Franklin County marriage license published in The Columbus Dispatch on 3 January 1971.

Has resided in Midland (Jefferson Township), Clinton County, Ohio with her husband Kalvis Danenbergs since at least 28 September 1973 (when both registered to vote in Clinton County; also signed a 31 July 2010 Toledo Blade guest-book entry from Midland, Ohio), raising their son Justin there from his birth on 1975 until he left for college in Columbus in 1994, teaching school for 40 years, and serving as local-history columnist for the Wilmington News Journal and Secretary of the Jefferson Township School Alumni & Friends association.
Born 24 February 1866 Jul. (8 March 1866 Greg.) at the Jāņmuiža watermill ('Jāņmuižas dzirnavās'), where her father Jānis Sirlaks worked as the miller.
Grew up at Kalna Vīstuči on the Jaunrauna estate after her father Jānis Sirlaks bought the farm in 1869.

Probably the 'Minna geb. Sirlak' recorded at the Smurģi farm in Jaunrauna (Rauna births 1890 no. 109, LVVA f. 235, apr. 7, l. 517, image 452) as mother of Emil Smurge, with her brother Reinhold Sirlak and father Jahn Sirlak standing as godparents.
Born 17 January 1916 in the rented house in the Vinterkalns area outside Cēsis where her parents Mārtiņš Sirlaks and Emma Smukule first lived after leaving Rīga in 1914.

Grew up at her parents' house at [address omitted] in Cēsis and attended the Bērzaine secondary school for four years alongside her sisters Elvīra (I0006, who left Cēsis for Rīga in autumn 1930) and Biruta (I0020).
Reported 'Rīga Vidzeme Latvia' as her residence on 1 January 1938 on her 23 July 1945 Haunstetten DP-2 registration card, working in Latvia as a nurse ('Sister of charity | Sanatorium, Latvia').

Arrived in Augsburg on 30 October 1944 as a refugee nurse ('Krankenschwester', 'Flüchtling', residing privately at Frauentorstraße 26 from 30.10.44 and receiving residence permit Nr. I.A. 006853 for Stadt u. Ldkr. Augsburg on 10 December 1944 valid to 1 January 1946; also stationed as a civilian worker in Burgau, Landkreis Günzburg in Schwaben from 15 April 1945 to 1 August 1945) before joining her mother and sisters at the Haunstetten DP camp in Augsburg.

Registered on 23 July 1945 at the Haunstetten DP camp in Augsburg (Reg. No. 902673064), living there with her mother and sisters until departing Haunstetten on 28 December 1948 under the Munich Hospital Domestics scheme and embarking on SS Scythia via Bremen-Grohn for Canada on 13–14 January 1949.

Settled in Montreal, Quebec upon arriving in Canada in January 1949; listed alongside her first cousin Velta Sirlaka (I1009) on the Montreal Latvian Relief Society roll, though her 6 April 1950 US border-crossing card at Detroit (for a 10-day visit to her mother Emma Sirlaka in Rockford, Ohio) records that Mirdza resided as a nurse's aide at 2475 Quesnel St., Montreal while Velta lived separately c/o the Homeopathic Hospital, Montreal.

Married the mathematics teacher Fricis Gailītis in Toronto in May 1955 and lived with him in Toronto until his death in September 1969 (joined from 1965/1969-09 by her mother Emma Sirlaka, who lived with them in Toronto until her death on 9 October 1970).

After her husband Fricis's death, she lived in her own apartment in West Bloomfield, Oakland County, Michigan (near her sister Biruta Balka), joining the Detroit Daugavas Vanagi branch in early 1990 before returning to Canada after retirement.
Returned after retirement to Windsor, Ontario (across the Detroit River from Michigan), where she lived until her sudden death on 5 July 2010 aged 94.

Born 2007 in California to Peter Charles Danenberg Jr. and Genevieve Elisa Symanski Nelson (married 10 September 2006), who are recorded together at their residence in Altadena, Los Angeles County, California in the US Public Records Index (11 May 2006, distinct from her paternal grandparents' Altadena house) and in Genevieve's Spokeo location history.

Childhood home in Monrovia, Los Angeles County, California with her mother Genevieve (whose Spokeo capture records a Monrovia condominium from 2012 to 2020, while her father lived in nearby Pasadena from 2011 to 2013/2014 and then in Mountain View).
Lived with her mother Genevieve in Alhambra, Los Angeles County, California (recorded in the Spokeo capture from 2019 to 2022).

Resides with her mother Genevieve at her current condominium in Monrovia, Los Angeles County, California (recorded from 2020 in the Spokeo capture, while her father moved from Mountain View to Palo Alto in September 2022, where Genevieve also has an undated public-records link).

Born 21 September / 3 October 1848 and baptised 26 September / 8 October 1848 at Kalna-Podis / Podiņi ('Freudenb. K. Pohdin', Cēsis rural births 1848 no. 135) to farmhand Mārcis Gibboy and Anne before the family moved to Farm XIV Luste by September 1850.

Born in 1849 and enumerated on 13/25 September 1850 in the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 291) at Farm XIV Luste (enclosed by P-priekuli) as 'dessen Sohn Marz, 1849 nachgeboren, 1½' with his parents Mārcis Gibboy (43) and Anne (31); the 1857 Priekuļi soul revision for Luste (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 27) records that he died in 1853 ('dessen Sohn Marz, 1½, starb 1853').

Born c. 1807 on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate; enumerated at age 5 in August 1811 at Farm No. 6 Ģiboļi ('No 6. Gibboÿ Gesinde') with his father Pēteris Ģibols (46), and at age 9 in early 1816 at Farm No. 21 Žvīguri ('21 Schwigur') after his father's death.

Lived at Podiņi farm no. 16 / XVI on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate in the 1826 soul revision (aged 19, with his first wife Marija, aged 35, and his father Pēteris Ģibols I1282's entry, who died in 1821) and in the 1834 soul revision (aged 27, with his first wife Marija, 31, and son Jānis I1299, born c. 1831, aged 3, who is later recorded aged 26 on the forest guards' and tax-liable lists on frames 48 and 54 of the 1857 Priekuļi soul revision), before moving to Luste farm no. XIV ('aus No. XVI') by 1850.

Married his second wife Anne in Priekuļi in October 1847 and was enumerated on 13/25 September 1850 in the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 112, image 291; 1857 list image 27) as a farmhand ('Knecht[?]') at Farm XIV Luste (enclosed by P-priekuli), aged 43, having come from Podiņi no. XVI, with his wife Anne (31) and their infant son Mārcis (born 1849, aged 1½, died 1853).

Worked as a Latvian farmhand ('Lett. Kn. Mahrzis Gibboij') at the Kalna-Podis farm ('Freudenberg K. Pohdis') on the Priekuļi estate when his daughter Marija was born there on 6/18 August 1853 and baptised in the Cēsis Latvian rural congregation on 16/28 August 1853.

Enumerated on 23 November / 5 December 1857 in the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 16) at Farm VI Rauguļi ('VI. Raugul Gesinde'), aged 50 ('aus No. XIV'), with his wife Anne (38) and daughters Marija (4) and Kristīne (2).

Born c. 1821/1822 to the manor weaver Jahn Sillak and Masche, and enumerated at age 12 on 11 May 1834 in the Jaunrauna soul revision (LVVA f. 199, apr. 1, l. 376, image 156) at Farm XXIX Lejas-Spāriņi ('Leis Sparing', Family 4), where his younger brother Jānis was born in May 1829 and his father died in 1830.

Moved from Farm XXIX Lejas-Spāriņi ('aus No. XXIX') to Farm XIV Vīstuči ('Wihstuz') on the Jaunrauna estate upon marrying Anne (widow of the farmer Peter Wihstuz, who died in 1843), had their son Pēteris Sirlaks there on 10/22 August 1847, and was enumerated at Vīstuči in the 9 October 1850 soul revision (Family 15, aged 28, with wife Anne, 43, son Peter, 2, stepson Dahw Wihstuz, 9, and stepdaughter Leene Wihstuz, 18) and the 8 February 1858 soul revision (Family 15/95, aged 36, with wife Anne, 51, son Peter, 10, and stepson Dahw Wihstuz, 14).

Recorded in the 1857 Priekuļi (Freudenberg) soul revision (LVVA f. 77, apr. 14, l. 344, image 32) at Farm XIX Ģiboļi ('XIX. Gibboi-Gesinde', enclosed by P-priekuli) as head of the farm ('Jahns Söhne 1. Marz Gibboi Wirth'), aged 34½ at the 1850 revision and 41½ in 1857 (born c. 1816), living there with his wife Anne (aged 38, identified in Raimonds Voroņins's tree as Anna Balodis, married 1843), his younger brother Jānis and Jānis's wife Anne, and his younger brother Dāvis (who was transferred to the Rīga tax roll in 1856).

Born 30 October 1883 Jul. (11 November 1883 Greg.) and baptised 26 December 1883 Jul. (7 January 1884 Greg.) at Lejas Vīstuči ('Neuhof, Lj. Wihstuz') in Jaunrauna as the fourth child of Pēteris Sirlaks and Marija Gibboja, and grew up at Vīstuči (where his eldest sister Natālija I1007 died on 14 June 1887 aged 12 and his father Pēteris I0007 died on 22 November 1896 when Mārtiņš was 13) before moving to Rīga.

Married Emma Smukule at St Martin's Lutheran church in Torņakalns, Rīga on 22 April 1911 Jul. (5 May 1911 Greg.), had their first daughter Elvīra there on 9 January 1912 (where he is recorded as a trader, 'торговецъ'), and lived in Torņakalns while keeping a tavern until World War I broke out in 1914.
Left Rīga at the start of World War I in 1914 and lived first in a rented house in the Vinterkalns area outside Cēsis, where his second daughter Mirdza was born on 17 January 1916.

By 1919 he and his wife Emma bought a house at Lielā Katrīnas iela 13 in Cēsis (where their third daughter Biruta was born on 3 June 1919 and the family survived the 1919 flu), opened a teahouse in Rožu laukums, and ran a grocery shop ('Sirlaks, M., pārtikas pr. tirgot., l. Katrinas ielā 13' in the 1924 trade directory; 'tirgotājs Sirlaks' in the 1927 Cēsu Avīze); daughter Elvīra (I0006) lived there until moving to Rīga in autumn 1930 for university (later running the Litene pharmacy in 1940/1941–1942) and daughters Mirdza (I0018) and Biruta (I0020) lived there until moving to Rīga by 1 January 1938, while Mārtiņš remained in Cēsis with Emma until his death from diabetes on 30 December 1942 aged 59.

Lived at Kalna Vīstuči (Emīļmāja) in Jaunrauna as the wife of Reinholds Sirlaks (where her parents-in-law Jānis I1026 and Līze I1027 lived until their deaths on 5 March 1901 and 6 January 1902), mother of Emīlis Sirlaks ('Emīļmāte' in Aina Jurciņa's memoir, p. 38), mother-in-law of Elza (I1271, married 1930), and grandmother of Harijs (I1272, born 11 January 1932) until the family was deported from Vīstuči on 25 March 1949 (case no. 12349).

Deported on 25 March 1949 aged 80 with her husband Reinholds (who died in April 1949), son Emīlis, daughter-in-law Elza, and grandson Harijs from Vīstuči to Chainsky district ('Tomskas apg. Čajas raj.'), Tomsk oblast, Siberia (case no. 12349), where she remained in forced settlement until her release on 2 July 1956.

Returned from Siberia after her release on 2 July 1956 with her son Emīlis and daughter-in-law Elza to Kalna Vīstuči in Jaunrauna, where she died on 21 June 1958 aged 89 and was buried in the Sirlaks family plot (001-147) at Jaunrauna cemetery.

Born 22 February 1875 Jul. (6 March 1875 Greg.) and baptised 9/21 March 1875 at Vīstuči ('Ronneburg-Neuhof, Lijas Wihstutschi') as the eldest child of Pēteris Sirlaks and Marija Gibboja, living there with her parents until her death in June 1887 aged 12.
Born 2018 in Rīga as the son of Einārs Dzirjānis and Inga Voroņina, and lives there with his parents and older sister Luīze.
