stays.note: Born 1978 in Los Angeles, California to Peter Valentins Danenbergs and Kathleen Diane Hall while both parents worked at the University of Southern California, before the family moved to nearby La Cañada Flintridge.

Childhood home in La Cañada Flintridge, Los Angeles County, California with his parents and sister Līga (recorded on his mother in the MyHeritage family tree while Līga attended nearby Glendale High School through 1984) before the family moved to Pasadena by 1 January 1988.

Lived with his parents in Pasadena, Los Angeles County, California from at least 1 January 1988 (when he was nine years old and his mother's Pasadena apartment is recorded in the US Public Records Index) before the family moved to nearby Altadena.
Lived with his parents and sister at his parents' longtime home in Altadena, Los Angeles County, California before beginning undergraduate studies at USC in 1995.

Completed his undergraduate studies at the University of Southern California in Los Angeles (1995–2000), earning a B.A. in Computer Science, Classics, Philosophy, German, and Piano and serving as student representative to the USC Board of Trustees.
Studied at Harvard University in Cambridge, Massachusetts as a Ph.D. candidate and research fellow in Comparative Literature from 2000 to 2002.
Studied at the University of Freiburg (Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany) as a Ph.D. candidate in Philosophy from 2002 to 2004.

Returned to the University of Southern California in Los Angeles in 2004 for graduate studies in Computer Science (earning an M.S. and pursuing a Ph.D. through 2008) and worked as a Research Assistant at USC's Information Sciences Institute from 2005.

Recorded in the US Public Records Index (in the MyHeritage GEDCOM) at a residence in Altadena, Los Angeles County, California on 11 May 2006 with his first wife Genevieve E. Danenberg (married 10 September 2006; daughter Mneme born 2007), where his mother Kathleen D. Danenberg is listed as an associated relative (while his parents lived at a separate house in Altadena, where Spokeo also links Genevieve with Peter and Līga), while continuing at USC (to 2008) and working at Response Genetics in Los Angeles (2008–2011).

Lived in Pasadena, Los Angeles County, California (where Shayla's public-records history places their apartment from November 2011), co-founded CrossFit Crown City (2011–2014, coaching five classes a day, seven days a week), and played for the Pasadena Rugby Football Club after marrying Shayla Nadah Alamdari on 14 February 2011.

Moved with Shayla and their children to Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California after joining Google in 2013; the 17 December 2015 Palo Alto Weekly feature and Shayla's Etsy profile describe the family as Mountain View residents before their September 2022 move to Palo Alto.

Moved with Shayla and their children to a townhouse in Palo Alto, Santa Clara County, California in September 2022 (subsequently purchased in July 2024 per property records in TruePeopleSearch), corroborated by his LinkedIn and GitHub profiles, the 15 January 2025 Marquis Who's Who press release datelined Palo Alto, and Shayla's 2025–2026 CrossFit Palo Alto affiliation.

Born 1942 in Rīga, Latvia to Arvīds Danenbergs and Elvīra Sirlaka (recorded on his 1945 Haunstetten DP-2 card, his parents' 1950 Declarations of Intention, and Latvju enciklopēdija, though the 1947 Regensburg list gives 'Schwanenberg' / Gulbene near his mother's Litene pharmacy), spending his infancy in Latvia (with his mother working at the Torņakalns pharmacy in Rīga and earlier at Litene, his father working in Talsi, and in 1944 staying with his mother, grandmother Emma, aunt Biruta, Vitolds Balks, and father on the Kurzeme coast and in Ventspils) until the family fled to Germany in autumn 1944.

Fled Latvia at age two in autumn 1944 with his parents and grandmother Emma via the Kurzeme coast, Ventspils, and Danzig to two farms in Landkreis Regensburg, Bavaria (listed on the 1947 Landkreis Regensburg foreigner list with sojourn date 12 January 1945), remaining there until summer 1945.

Lived with his parents, grandmother Emma, aunt Biruta, uncle Vitolds, cousin Ilze, and twin siblings Kalvis and Līga (born 1946) in the Latvian DP camp at Haunstetten near Augsburg (where his aunt Mirdza was also registered from 23 July 1945 until emigrating to Canada in December 1948 / January 1949), attending the camp's Latvian kindergarten until the family departed Haunstetten on 21 June 1949 for the Bremen-Grohn port transit camp (21–28 June 1949).

After landing in Boston on 7 July 1949, he lived with his parents, twin siblings, and grandmother on the farm of sponsor Robert M. Hawk in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio (Rockford mailing address, where the Balks family joined them in late January / February 1950), starting school and enumerated there in the 10 April 1950 US Census.

Moved with his family after about a year on the Hawk farm to Tiffin, Seneca County, Ohio (where his parents are recorded in 1953, 1956, 1958, and 1959 Tiffin city directories while his mother worked as a pharmacist at Mercy Hospital in Tiffin and his father bought a Seneca County farm in 1955), attending Hopewell-Loudon School in nearby Bascom, Seneca County (pictured in eighth grade in the 1956 yearbook and ninth grade in the 1957 yearbook).
Attended Case Institute of Technology in Cleveland, Ohio, graduating with a B.S. in chemistry in 1964.

Moved to Los Angeles in 1964 to pursue graduate studies in organic chemistry (M.S. conferred 1967) and work as an assistant at the University of Southern California; married Kathleen Diane Hall in Los Angeles on 23 April 1966 and lived with her there until moving to Santa Barbara before 18 October 1966.

Lived in Santa Barbara, California with his wife Kathleen while working as a research assistant and earning his Ph.D. in bioorganic chemistry (1970) at the University of California, Santa Barbara; their daughter Līga was born in Santa Barbara on 1966.

Lived in Madison, Wisconsin with his wife and daughter while working as a postdoctoral researcher at the McArdle Laboratory for Cancer Research (1970–1974) and scientist at the University of Wisconsin Clinical Cancer Center (1974–1976).

Returned to Los Angeles in 1976 to join the Department of Biochemistry faculty at the USC School of Medicine; co-authored papers with Kathleen at USC in 1977–1978 and had their son Peter in Los Angeles on 1978 before settling in nearby La Cañada Flintridge.

Resided with his family in La Cañada Flintridge, Los Angeles County, California (recorded on Kathleen in the MyHeritage family tree while daughter Līga attended nearby Glendale High School, graduating in 1984) before moving to Pasadena by 1 January 1988.
Resided in Pasadena, Los Angeles County, California from at least 1 January 1988 while serving on the USC School of Medicine faculty.

Resided in Altadena, Los Angeles County, California (named as 'Peter Danenbergs of Altadena, Calif.' in his father's February 1996 obituaries and recorded in the MyHeritage tree and on Kathleen's 2007–2012 SEC EDGAR filings; son Peter lived there until 1995 and daughter Līga until 1 September 1996) until their house was destroyed in the Eaton Fire of 7–8 January 2025.
After losing their Altadena home in the January 2025 Eaton Fire, his wife Kathleen lists Los Angeles, California on her verified LinkedIn profile in 2026.
Born 14 December 1908 (date recorded in the Social Security Death Index) to Melvin Porter Nolen and Addie Lee Foley, with his provenance recorded as Monroe City, Missouri in the 2015 database.

Married Berniece Wilmina Holt and had their daughter Carol May Nolen in 1934, whose provenance in the 2015 database is Grand Junction, Mesa County, Colorado (and his Social Security number was issued in Colorado).
Resided at the end of his life in Los Angeles, Los Angeles County, California (ZIP 90015), where the Social Security Death Index records his last known residence at his death in January 1985 aged 76.

Born 10 August 1847 Jul. (22 August 1847 Greg.) at Farm XIV Vīstuči ('Neuhof Wihstuz') on the Jaunrauna estate to Mārcis Sirlaks and Anne (widow Vīstucis), enumerated there in the 1850 (aged 2) and 1858 (aged 10) soul revisions, and bought the Lejas Vīstuči homestead on instalments from the manor lord August Joachim von Pander in 1872.

Farmed as owner ('Landesbesitzer' / 'Wirth' / 'хозяинъ') at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna with his wife Marija Gibboja (whom he married at Rauna church on 10/22 February 1874) and their eight children born at Vīstuči between 1875 and 1895 (of whom eldest daughter Natālija I1007 died on 14 June 1887 aged 12; Marija's sister Kristīne I1302 also resided at Lejas Vīstuči as the wife of mason Jānis Karnītis in 1883/1888-06-10), also serving as local correspondent for Mājas Viesis until his death from cancer at Vīstuči on 10/22 November 1896 aged 49 years 3 months.
Born 1953 in Straupe, Latvia, where his parents Vasilijs Voroņins (1924–1962) and Zenta Mežviete (1926–2021) lived before moving to Rauna (voronins-tree.ged lines 31–33, 270–271, 324).

Moved in childhood with his parents from Straupe to Rauna (where his father Vasilijs Voroņins was buried in Rauna cemetery after dying in November 1962) and grew up in Rauna until his marriage on 11 June 1977.

Married Velta Stangaine in Rauna on 11 June 1977 and lived with her in Rauna, where they raised their children Raimonds (I1053, born 1978 in Cēsis, who writes 'Visu savu bērnību esmu pavadījis Raunā', I spent my entire childhood in Rauna, before moving to Rīga in 1996/2017), Inga (I1242, born 1981 in Rīga, who moved to Rīga in 1998/2013), and Līva (I1248, born 1990 in Cēsis, whom Aina Jurciņa visited on foot in Rauna on her second birthday on [day omitted] 1992 and who grew up in Rauna to 1998/2008), and took part in the 1993–1998 family work-parties restoring Lejas Vīstuči in nearby Jaunrauna.

Born c. 1765 on the Priekuļi (Freudenberg) estate (aged 30 in 1795 and 46 in August 1811); enumerated in August 1811 at Farm No. 6 Ģiboļi ('No 6. Gibboÿ Gesinde', enclosed by P-priekuli) with his son Mārcis (aged 5), and recorded at Farm No. 19 Ģibaiņi ('19 Gibbain') in the 1816 Priekuļi soul revision as 'Knecht Peter Ansche Sohn, 46 — gestorben' (died between 1811 and 1816).

Born 1978 in the maternity hospital at the district seat of Cēsis to Pēteris Voroņins and Velta Stangaine, and spent his entire childhood in Rauna ('Visu savu bērnību esmu pavadījis Raunā, tāpēc varētu teikt, ka tā ir mana dzimtā puse', voronins-tree.ged line 124) with his parents and younger sisters Inga (I1242, born 1981) and Līva (I1248, born 1990), helping in 1995–1997 with the family work-parties restoring his great-grandfather Dāvis Sirlaks's farm Lejas Vīstuči in nearby Jaunrauna.

Moved after childhood to Rīga, where he currently resides ('Šobrīd esmu pilntiesīgs rīdzinieks'; RESI Rīga, Latvija in voronins-tree.ged lines 110–115, 124) and has raised his daughters Anna Voroņina (I1263) and Emīlija Voroņina (I1264, with Inga Jansone I1243) and Agnese Voroņina (I1265, with Līga Liepiņa I1235).

Born 8 September 1862 Jul. (20 September 1862 Greg.) and baptised 23 September / 5 October 1862 at the Jāņmuiža watermill ('Johannenhof Mühle') in Cēsis rural parish, where his father Jānis Sirlaks worked as the miller ('Müller Jahnis Sirlak') and where his younger sister Minna was born in 1866.
Grew up at Kalna Vīstuči on the Jaunrauna estate after his father Jānis Sirlaks bought the farm in 1869 (where his sisters Ernestīne I1028 and Minna I1030 lived until 1869/1880 and 1869/1890).

Succeeded his father at Kalna Vīstuči (Emīļmāja) in Jaunrauna (where his father Jānis I1026 died on 5 March 1901 and his mother Līze I1027 died on 6 January 1902), farming there with his wife Mīle (née Upīte, I1031), their children (including son Emīlis I1032, born 1900), daughter-in-law Elza (I1271, married 1930), and grandson Harijs (I1272, born 11 January 1932) until the entire household was deported on 25 March 1949 (case no. 12349).
Deported on 25 March 1949 aged 86 with his family from Vīstuči to Chainsky district (Čajas rajons), Tomsk oblast, Siberia (case no. 12349), where he died four weeks later on 20 or 22 April 1949.
Born c. 1922 in Washington (age 8 in the 1930 census, age 18 in the 1940 census, age 20 on his June 1942 Clark County marriage return) to Charles W. Helgerson and Lola Lucille Alderson.
Lived with his parents at [address omitted], Portland, Oregon in the 1928 Portland city directory before the family moved to Los Angeles.
Enumerated at age 8 with his parents Charles W. and Lola L. Helgerson and aunt Carrie M. Alderson in Los Angeles, Los Angeles County, California in the April 1930 census.

Returned with his parents to Portland, Oregon by February 1933 (grandfather Winter Scott Alderson's funeral notice) and enumerated with them in Tract 52, Portland in the 1940 census (which records their 1935 residence in the same place) through his marriage on 20 June 1942.

Born in October 1985 in Southern California to Fathollah Alamdari and Jeanne Marie Kerbrat (married 20 April 1985 in Los Angeles); her father's TruePeopleSearch capture places the family at a residence in Monrovia, Los Angeles County, California in November–December 1985 before moving to La Verne in October 1986.

Raised with her parents in La Verne, Los Angeles County, California, where she graduated from Bonita High School in the Class of 2003, her father's TruePeopleSearch capture records two La Verne residences from October 1986 to June 2018, and her own TruePeopleSearch capture records her parents' La Verne house from January 2003 to July 2004 (after she turned 18) and her 909 area-code phone numbers (alongside a Mountain View apartment record from July 2004 to October 2014).

Married Peter Charles Danenberg Jr. on 14 February 2011 and lived with him and their first two children (Kairos, born 2012, and Arete, born 2013) at an apartment in Pasadena, Los Angeles County, California (recorded on her TruePeopleSearch profile from November 2011) while Peter ran CrossFit Crown City (2011–2014).

Moved with her husband and children to Mountain View, Santa Clara County, California after Peter joined Google in 2013; the 17 December 2015 Palo Alto Weekly feature interviews her as 'Mountain View resident Shayla Danenberg' with her husband and four children, corroborated by Mountain View on her Etsy profile.

Moved with her husband and children to a townhouse in Palo Alto, Santa Clara County, California in September 2022 (subsequently purchased in July 2024 per property records in TruePeopleSearch), where she trains and competes at CrossFit Palo Alto (2025–2026).

Every census and her children's birth certificates give her birthplace as Ireland (the 1930 and 1940 censuses say Northern Ireland; the 2015 family tree says Dublin, which is unverified in the Irish civil register). The 1920 census gives her immigration year as 1898 and the 1930 census gives 1903.

Lived in Vancouver, Clark County, Washington with her husband Charles Henry Hall: their three children Margaret Ellen (6 Jan 1919), Charles Henry (11 Jun 1920) and Catherine (12 Feb 1922, born at home) were born there, and she was enumerated there as Susie A. Hall on 7 January 1920. On the 1920 census (7 January, ED 36, sheet 8A, lines 14–16) the household lived at 112 Fourteenth Street, Vancouver (read from the whole census sheet, 2026-11-09).

Moved across the Columbia River to Portland, Oregon by April 1930, where she headed her household with her three children in 1930, lived with her daughter Catherine in 1935, 1940 and 1950, and died on 6 February 1972. The 1930 census (7 April 1930, ED 26-472, sheet 2A) has them at 1225 S. Leonard Street, St. Johns, Portland; the 1950 census (13 April 1950, ED 37-553, sheet 6, lines 10–11) at 9727 N. Willamette Blvd., in the same house as in April 1949 (both read from the whole census sheets, 2026-11-09).

Born 1963 in Los Angeles County, California (California Birth Index, Mother's Maiden Name: Leslie) to John Grattan Fitz Gibbon Sr. and Lael Leslie before moving to Somerset, New Jersey with his mother and stepfather James Lepowsky.

Born 1963 to John Grattan Fitz Gibbon Sr. and Lael Leslie, with his provenance recorded in the 2015 database as Somerset, Somerset County, New Jersey, where he grew up with his mother Lael Leslie and stepfather James Lepowsky (professor of mathematics at nearby Rutgers University in New Brunswick; it is unknown whether he was born in California/Oregon before moving to New Jersey or whether his adopted half-sister Mei Lepowsky's years in the household overlapped with his).

Born in Latvia in September 1938 (recorded as 20 September 1938 in the MyHeritage family tree and his 2019 obituary index, whereas the US Public Records Index gives 1 September 1938) before emigrating to the United States.

Resided in Beverly Hills, Oakland County, Michigan with his wife Ilze Balka and their daughters Inga (born 1971) and Ivete (born 1973), recorded there in the US Public Records Index on both his and Ilze's entries (Ilze is recorded in Farmington from 1 October 1992, while daughter Ivete is recorded at the Beverly Hills address on 1 February 1994).

Recorded in the US Public Records Index as residing in Farmington, Oakland County, Michigan, with entries in [address omitted] on 1 July 2004 and 2 November 2004, a separate Farmington/Farmington Hills telephone number from 1 January 1984 to 25 March 2008, and named as 'John Augenbergs of Farmingham [Farmington], MI' in his mother Vera Augenbergs's 7 December 2008 Indianapolis obituary.
Resided in adjacent Farmington Hills, Oakland County, Michigan, where his obituary records his death on 23 February 2019 aged 80.

Born 4 March 1947 as the elder son of Alberts Jurciņš (I1014, who died in late 1953) and Aina Modrīte Sirlaka (I1010, who moved to Jaunpiebalga in 1953/1963) at the Jurciņš family farm 'Zvirgzdiņi' in Jaungulbene parish (Gulbene district; younger brother Alfrēds I1228 grew up there until 1965/1970), where he and his wife Ņina Panšina (I1256, married by 1978-09-26) recovered the family cowshed when the kolkhozes were liquidated in 1991–1993 and raised their children Māris (I1240, born 1978) and Alīna (I1246, born 1987, who married in Gulbene on 30 June 2017); he died on 4 September 2019 aged 72.

Born Sunday 28 September 1924 in the downstairs room of the old house at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna as the fifth and youngest child of Dāvis Sirlaks and Alma Leontīne Āboltiņa, growing up at Vīstuči (where his paternal grandmother Marija I0008 died on 1 November 1925 and his maternal aunt Zelma Āboltiņa I1045 moved in 1929/1930) while attending the 4-year Dievabērns school in Jaunrauna and grades 5–6 at Rauna parish school.

Studied at Priekuļi Agricultural Secondary School ('Priekuļu Lauksaimniecības vidusskola') before his wartime conscription into the Latvian Legion (during which he was hospitalised in Cēsis with pleurisy).
Studied at the Jelgava Agricultural Academy ('Jelgavas Lauksaimniecības akadēmija'), where his sister Ilga brought him provisions from Vīstuči and where he earned his degree as a mechanical engineer.

Worked as chief engineer of the Priekuļi Plant Breeding and Selection Station ('Priekuļu selekcijas galvenais inženieris'), marrying Valda Katlapa and raising their children Jānis (born 1956) and Inga (born 1959, who left Priekuļi in 1977 to study medicine in Rīga).

Led the family's return to Lejas Vīstuči beginning on 1 May 1993, living at first alone in the barn loft and the small barn room (fitted with a stove in winter 1994, 'Toreiz viņš tur vēl dzīvoja viens, ģimene vēl nebija piepulcējusies', memoir p. 45, while his wife Valda and son Jānis helped rebuild and later moved into their finished upstairs rooms at Christmas 1995), hoisting the Latvian flag at Vīstuči on 17 November 1993, celebrating his 70th birthday there on 8 September 1994, and returning from a Rīga hospital stay for pancreatitis (August 1995) to die at Vīstuči at 1:08 a.m. in the night of 11/12 October 1995 aged 71.

Born at Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna in September 1918 (recorded as 19 September 1918 on her 1947 IRO Resettlement Record citing a 19 May 1932 birth certificate no. 421 from the clergyman of Rauna and in her 2015 obituary, and as 3 September 1918 in her sister Aina's memoir) as the second child of Dāvis Sirlaks and Alma Leontīne Āboltiņa, growing up at Vīstuči (where her aunt Kristīne I1035 is last recorded in June 1919, her paternal grandmother Marija I0008 died on 1 November 1925, and her maternal aunt Zelma Āboltiņa I1045 moved in 1929/1930) while attending the 4-year Dievabērns school in Jaunrauna and grades 5–6 at Rauna parish school.

Attended secondary school at Cēsis State Gymnasium, where her mother placed her in lodgings in Cēsis with 'Madame Sahner' so that she would learn German and her brother Valdis drove provisions to her from Vīstuči.

Graduated from the Red Cross Sisters of Mercy nursing school ('Žēlsirdīgo māsu skola') in Rīga, began university studies, and worked as an ophthalmic nurse at the 1st City Hospital in Rīga until departing Rīga on 9 August 1944 ('RIGA 9.VIII.1944' on her 1947 IRO Resettlement Record).

Refugee nurse in Schleswig-Holstein in the British Zone of Germany after leaving Rīga on 9 August 1944, receiving DP registration document DPJC G21001248 in Lübeck on 28 November 1945 (No. E. 13189) and residing at the Mürwik DP camp (Centre 1203) in Flensburg when she signed her IRO Resettlement Record on 25 November 1947.

Emigrated to Canada in 1948 and lived in Montreal, Quebec, where she is recorded on the membership roll of the Montreal Latvian Relief Society and named on her first cousin Mirdza Sirlaka's 6 April 1950 US border-crossing card at Detroit as Mirdza's nearest relative in Canada at 'c/o Homeopathic Hosp. Montreal' (while Mirdza lived separately at 2475 Quesnel St., Montreal).

Married Jānis Grīslis in the Latvian Lutheran congregation in Hamilton, Ontario in June 1955 (reported in Latvija Amerikā on 22 June 1955) and lived with him in their own house in Ontario (also wintering in Florida).

Lived in her later years in St. Catharines, Ontario, where she died at Tufford Manor Nursing Home on 12 March 2015 in her 97th year (three years after her husband Jānis's death on 1 April 2012), with her funeral held at Hulse & English Funeral Home & Chapel on Church Street in St. Catharines.
Born 1955 and raised in Jaunpiebalga, Latvia by her parents Arvīds Stangainis and Ilga Laimdota Sirlaka alongside her older sister Ilze.

Married Pēteris Voroņins in Rauna on 11 June 1977 and lived with him in Rauna, where they raised their children Raimonds (I1053, born 1978 in the maternity hospital at Cēsis, who writes in voronins-tree.ged line 124 'Visu savu bērnību esmu pavadījis Raunā', I spent my entire childhood in Rauna, before moving to Rīga in 1996/2017), Inga (I1242, born 1981 in Rīga, who moved to Rīga in 1998/2013), and Līva (I1248, born 1990 in Cēsis, whom Aina Jurciņa visited on foot from Priekuļi to Rauna and back on her second birthday on [day omitted], memoir p. 54, and who grew up in Rauna to 1998/2008), and took part in the 1993–1998 family work-parties restoring Lejas Vīstuči in nearby Jaunrauna.

Born 16 June 1921 in Vecpiebalga, Vidzeme, Latvia to Žanis Balks and Elza Brauns[?], as self-reported on his 23 July 1945 Haunstetten DP-2 registration card and recorded on the 1947 Landkreis Kelheim foreigner list.

Reported Rīga, Latvia as his residence on 1 January 1938 on his 1945 Haunstetten DP-2 card, where he graduated from the Church Gymnasium, began studying engineering at the University of Latvia, and worked as an office clerk in a food supplies department.

After meeting Biruta ('Rūta') Sirlaka on the Kurzeme coast in autumn 1944, deserting from his German army (Latvian Legion) unit, and fleeing with her and the Danenberg/Sirlaks family via Ventspils and Danzig to Bavaria, he and Biruta were assigned to wartime farm labour in Landkreis Kelheim (about a 30-minute train ride from the Danenbergs' farm in Landkreis Regensburg, recorded for 1945 on the 17 June 1947 Landkreis Kelheim foreigner list); in spring 1945 they drove by horse and wagon into Regensburg to marry before moving to the Haunstetten DP camp in July 1945.

Registered on 23 July 1945 at the Haunstetten DP camp near Augsburg, sharing a three-bedroom apartment with Biruta, their daughter Ilze (born 1945), Emma Sirlaka, and the Danenberg family (where sister-in-law Mirdza was registered from 23 July 1945 until emigrating to Canada in December 1948 / January 1949, and from which Emma and the five Danenbergs departed for the USA on 21–22 June 1949), remaining at Haunstetten with Biruta and Ilze until transferring to the Bremen-Grohn resettlement center on 9 January 1950.

Transferred from Assembly Center Haunstetten no. 505 on 9 January 1950 to the IRO Resettlement Center at Bremen-Grohn with his wife Biruta and daughter Ilze before sailing for New York on USS General Howze on 22 January 1950.

After arriving in New York on USS General Howze in late January / February 1950 (sponsored by J. Smalley, R. 3, Rockford, Ohio), he lived and worked as a farm hand in the shared household with the Danenbergs and Emma Sirlaka in Liberty Township, Mercer County, Ohio (enumerated there in the 10 April 1950 US Census, listed at Rockford, Ohio on Emma's 14 August 1950 Declaration of Intention, and in Ohio when Biruta applied for her Social Security number in February 1951).

Lived with his wife Biruta and daughter Ilze in the Southfield, Oakland County, Michigan area, where his mother-in-law Emma Sirlaka's US Social Security Death Index record gives her last US residence at ZIP code 48075 in Southfield (before Emma moved to Toronto in 1965/1969-09 and died in October 1970).

Settled with his wife Biruta in Oakland County, Michigan (Birmingham / Beverly Hills / West Bloomfield area, where daughter Ilze is recorded in Beverly Hills from 1 September 1973, his SSDI record gives his last residence at ZIP code 48010, and he ran his own engineering consulting firm in the Detroit area until his sudden death on 28 September 1984).
Born in March 1882 in California according to the 1900 US census (MMPL-98T) while his parents Edward and Harriet Newman were moving west from Kansas to Oregon.
Grew up with his parents and siblings in Fossil, Gilliam County, Oregon through the births of Lilly E. (1882/1884) and Grover Cleveland Newman (1886/1887) and Carrie May's August 1892 elopement.
Enumerated at age 18 (born March 1882 in California, single) in his parents' household in Toroda Creek Precinct, Okanogan County, Washington in the 1900 census.
Born c. 1813–1814 in Great Yarmouth, Norfolk, England according to the 1851 England census (SGBB-G9M) and FamilySearch tree 9KW4-JD9.

Settled in his wife Elizabeth Flower's parish of Freethorpe, Norfolk by 29 December 1839 (when their daughter Hariet was baptised there), had sons William (1842), Edward (1844), David, George and Charles (11 June 1854) baptised there, and was enumerated there as a master cooper in the 1851 census (SGBB-G9M); he was absent from the 1861 Freethorpe census household (M7X1-DM9).
Emigrated to Orleans County, New York and died in Yates, Orleans County, New York on 27 May 1890.
Born c. 1914–1916 in Oregon (age 19 at his 30 December 1933 marriage; age 24, born in Oregon, in the 1940 census).
Married Estella May Alderson of Portland on 30 December 1933 across the river in Vancouver, Washington, and the 1940 census records both their 1935 residences as Portland, Multnomah County, Oregon.

Enumerated in the 1940 census as head of household (Sherwin William Rowley, age 24) with his wife Stella May Rowley (age 23) in Concord Election Precinct, Clackamas County, Oregon (Sheet 5A, lines 13–14, Household 106), immediately next door to Stella's adoptive mother Carrie May Schroeder and Charles Schroeder (Sheet 5A, lines 11–12, Household 105).
Born 1 December 1866 in Springwater, Clackamas County, Oregon to Christopher Alderson and Mary Catharine Royal.
Enumerated at age 4 with his parents Christopher and Mary C. Alderson in Jackson County, Oregon in the 1870 census.
Enumerated at age 13 with his parents Christopher and Mary C. Alderson and his maternal grandmother Mary A. Royal in Sheridan, Yamhill County, Oregon in the 1880 census.
Eloped with Carrie May Newman from Fossil, Gilliam County, Oregon on 16 August 1892 and married her in Gilliam County on 4 September 1892.

His daughter Lola Lucille Alderson was born on 19 June 1893 in Oregon, with her Oregon birth records giving the county variously as Umatilla County (HR3B-1P2M) and Wheeler County (W7J8-HGN2; Wheeler County was created in 1899 from territory including Fossil).
His son Elmer Elsworth Alderson was born on 22 October 1895 in Portland, Oregon according to his Oregon birth record (84KN-27MM) and 1944 Oregon death certificate (ZNLQ-YFPZ).
Enumerated on 23 April 1910 in Milwaukie, Clackamas County, Oregon as head of household with his wife May C., children Lola (17) and Elmer (14), and mother-in-law Hattie Newman.

Lived in Portland from at least 1916 (voter registration at 446 East Salmon Street) through the 1920 census (222 East 7th Street), 1921 (5003 38th Street) and the 1930 census (5003 52nd Avenue S.E.) with Carrie and their adoptive daughter Estella, until his death in Portland on 27 February 1933.

Born 1944 in Bad Godesberg on the Rhine (now a district of Bonn, Germany) to Wolfgang Schubach and Annemarie Blum, and lived in Bad Breisig, Frankfurt, and near Mendig in the Rhineland during his youth until immigrating to the United States with his family in 1959.

Immigrated with his family in 1959 to the Cleveland, Ohio area, settling in the suburb of Beachwood (Cuyahoga County), where he graduated from Beachwood High School and then from John Carroll University in adjacent University Heights.

Listed as a player on the Columbus Germania soccer team in the Ohio-Indiana Soccer League in The Columbus Dispatch on 2 October 1966 (he also worked for the health department in Philadelphia before settling in Milwaukee with his wife Līga by 1969/1971).

Moved with his wife Liga Danenberg to Milwaukee, Wisconsin after their 1968/1969 marriage, where he worked as a computer programmer, co-founded EXACTA Corporation (1976, Brookfield) and Exacta Graphics, Inc. (1985, Butler), and lived for 50 years until his death in Milwaukee on 15 March 2019; his mother-in-law Elvīra Danenbergs (I0006) is also recorded at their Milwaukee home in the US Public Records Index during her Milwaukee years (1996/1998–2011).

Born 1924 to François (Frank) Kerbrat and Ozanna L'Herreaux (Ozanna Lheureux), who were living in Roseville, Macomb County, Michigan eighteen months later on 27 April 1926 when his younger brother Adrien F. Kerbrat was born in Roseville (though Yves's own NUMIDENT entry does not name his birthplace town).

Moved with his parents and brother Adrien from Michigan to the Santa Monica area of Los Angeles County, California, where he and Adrien were issued sequential California Social Security numbers (559-18-4795 and 559-18-4798) prior to his 1950–1952 Korean War US Army service and his parents filed Social Security claims at the Santa Monica field office in 1952 and 1956.

Lived with his wife Carol May Nolen and daughter Jeanne M. Kerbrat (born 1964 and married in Los Angeles on 20 April 1985) in the San Fernando Valley of Los Angeles — filing his Social Security claim at the Van Nuys office on 29 November 1975 and residing in Sylmar, Los Angeles (ZIP 91342) until his death on 16 February 1986.

people.name: Zelma Forstmane

stays.note: Resided with her husband Alberts Danenbergs in Stūrmuiža parish, Tukums district, Courland, Latvia (adjacent to Vecauce/Auce) when their son Arvīds Fricis Danenbergs was born there on 17 January 1913 (4 January 1913 Julian).

aka: Zelma née Forstmanis ('Forstmann' [?]), on her son Arvīds's DP card

stays.note: Born 2 October 1883 Jul. (14 October 1883 Greg.) at the Apiņi farm in Vecsalaca, Salaca parish (Raduraksti 1:4:11:2055:2487:24479, frame 23) to Ancis and Dārta Āboltiņš, and grew up with her parents and siblings at their family farm Ļekunkas in Salaca parish.

After her husband, the widower Aleksandrs ('Saša') Martinsons, drowned in a river, she moved c. 1929–1930 (when her niece Aina was in the 3rd grade) to her sister Alma and brother-in-law Dāvis Sirlaks's farm Lejas Vīstuči in Jaunrauna, dedicating 30 years ('30 Vīstučiem ziedoti gadi') as a second mother to their children (and living at nearby Kalna Gāles in Jaunrauna toward the end of her life after Dāvis had her struck off the Vīstuči register to reduce Soviet taxes) until dying in Ilga Sirlaka's care in 1960, one year after Alma.

Married Valdis Jurciņš and lived with him at the Jurciņš family farm 'Zvirgzdiņi' in Jaungulbene parish (Gulbene district), raising their children Māris (born 1978) and Alīna (born 1987) and cleaning out the returned cowshed at 'Zvirgzdiņi' when the kolkhozes were liquidated in 1991–1993.

Resided at the Dzērupi farmstead (P-dzerupi) in Penkule parish (P-penkule), Jelgava district, Latvia in September 1931 when Jaunā Zemgalieša pielikums (27 September 1931, p. 3) reported that 'Schanis [Žanis] Danenbergs no Penkules pagasta Dsehrup mahjam' scalded his leg while working at a threshing machine; two months earlier, in July 1931, his brother Arvīds graduated from the 2nd Jelgava State Gymnasium recorded as 'no Penkules'.

Remained in Latvia and was named as Arvīds Danenbergs's surviving brother in Latvia in his February–April 1996 US and Latvian exile-press obituaries; no record places him between September 1931 (in Penkule) and February 1996 (in Latvia), and the marriage and birth dates of his wife (I0010) and daughters Laima (I0110) and Irēna (I0111) in the 2015 family tree are unknown.

Recorded with Latvian provenance in the 2015 family tree as the wife of Arvīds Danenbergs's brother Žanis Danenbergs (who is documented in Penkule in September 1931 and surviving in Latvia in February 1996) and mother of Laima and Irēna Danenberga; her own birth, marriage, and death dates are unrecorded.
